papers.title_en: Fortuitous BMN Cohomology at Every $N$
papers.abstract_en: Finite-$N$ trace relations can produce $Q$-cohomology classes with no stable large-$N$ ancestor. The brane-fused construction at $SU(3)$ suggests that such states can retain an $SU(2)$ nonabelian core accompanied by scalar hair. We develop this idea into a general construction for every $SU(N)$, $N\geq3$. Starting from the $SU(2)$ threshold operator $O_{24}$, we select pairs of eigenvalues of one scalar and construct corrected two-colour letters whose $Q$-transformations obey the $SU(2)$ rules exactly. Substitution into $O_{24}$ gives a closed rational operator for each pair. Multiplying by eigenvalue-separation factors removes the denominators, and summing over all pairs produces a gauge-invariant polynomial. An exact block-restriction identity recovers a nonzero multiple of $O_{24}$. The restriction maps every stable class to a stable $SU(2)$ class, proving that the resulting operator is non-exact and fortuitous, even when non-Coulombic stable classes are included. This proves the existence of fortuitous BMN cohomology at every $N\geq3$. The construction is an exact algebraic realization of a nonabelian core with scalar dressing.

papers.title_en: Signatures of Dynes superconductivity in the THz response of ALD-grown NbN thin films
papers.abstract_en: The frequency-dependent complex optical conductivity reflects key properties of superconductors, such as the energy gap in the density of states (DOS) and the superfluid density. For disordered superconductors, the optical conductivity often can be described within Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) theory, while in corresponding tunneling experiments, deviations in the observed DOS typically require modelling by the phenomenological Dynes formula. The implications of such Dynes DOS for optics were rarely discussed so far. Here we probe the terahertz conductivity of superconducting NbN thin films with thicknesses ranging from 4.5 to 20nm, which were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD). Our frequency range from 0.3 to 2.1 THz covers energies below and above the spectral gap. For 20nm thick NbN, we find in the optical conductivity distinct deviations from the BCS model, including a step-like characteristic in the absorption at half the zero-temperature spectral gap. These observations can be fully captured by Dynes electrodynamics with a small and temperature-independent pair-breaking rate. For the other films, we also observe signs of Dynes electrodynamics, and we discuss the evolution of the energy gap, the superfluid density, and the pair-breaking rate as function of film thickness.

papers.title_en: Probing fundamental physics with ALMA2040 mm-wavelength observations of neutron stars
papers.abstract_en: Bursty or (rotation-induced) pulsed coherent radio emission from pulsars, magnetars, and fast radio transients originates in some of the most extreme environments in the Universe. However, the exact physical mechanism behind the scenes remains poorly understood. ALMA2040 will allow for systematic exploration of the millimeter-wavelength spectral window for pulsars and fast radio transients for the very first time, offering unprecedented opportunities to discover new observational phenomena and advance our understanding of emission physics. Beyond this, ALMA2040 provides a unique means to unveil the neutron-star population in the Galactic Centre (GC), enable novel tests of fundamental physics in the vicinity of the supermassive black hole Sgr A*, probe the potential existence of dark matter in the GC, and investigate the dense, highly dynamic interstellar and magnetic environment of this region.

papers.title_en: Augmentation curve for torus knots
papers.abstract_en: We prove a version of topological recursion for the correlation differentials of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials of torus knots on the corresponding augmentation curves, following the proposal of Gu, Jockers, Klemm, and Soroush. To this end, we explicitly construct the spectral curve from the so-called auxiliary curve of Brini, Eynard, and Mariño and prove that it coincides with the augmentation curve for every torus knot with coprime $(r,s)$. Finally, our version of topological recursion proves the higher-genus closed-string prediction of the Aganagic--Vafa conjecture for all torus knot augmentation curves.

papers.title_en: A Shell Collision Scenario for EP251222b/GRB 251222A: Connecting Prompt Emission and Double-Peaked Afterglow
papers.abstract_en: GRB 251222A is a long-duration gamma-ray burst at a spectroscopic redshift of $z=3.171$. It was detected by the EP as the soft X-ray transient EP251222b before and during the gamma-ray emission. We performed a multi-wavelength (EP/WXT, fermi/GBM, swift/XRT and optical/NIR) investigation of this event. Its prompt soft X-ray and gamma-ray features, together with two afterglow rebrightenings, allow us to examine a possible connection between the prompt ejecta and the afterglow. We consider a multiple-shell scenario in which a faster, narrower shell catches up with a slower, wider shell. We assume that the selected pulse groups trace different ejecta and that the late X-ray flare marks their collision. Under these assumptions, we represent the post-collision outflow by an effective merged core and an outer annular component. A joint fit to the multi-band afterglow gives a Lorentz factor of $Γ_c\approx293$ for the merged core and $Γ_{1,w}\approx228$ for the outer component. The sample-wise collision mapping gives an energy release of $E_{\rm diss}=(1.6^{+2.1}_{-0.9})\times10^{52}$ erg and a dynamical dissipation efficiency of $0.37^{+0.07}_{-0.14}\%$. EP251222b can therefore be used to test a prompt--afterglow connection through shell collisions, although it does not uniquely establish this interpretation.

papers.title_en: Flat-band ferrimagnetism in the edge-centered honeycomb antiferromagnet: From harmonic flat magnon to broad continuum
papers.abstract_en: One of the most striking aspects of a flat band is not merely its lack of dispersion, but that it reduces the single-particle kinetic energy to a very small scale, allowing interaction effects to become the dominant energy scale in the low-energy physics. This picture has underpinned concepts such as flat-band ferromagnetism, flat-band superconductivity, and localized magnons. A more fundamental question, however, remains. Flat bands belong to the language of single-particle or linear-spin-wave physics; whether they survive as protected sharp excitations in a genuine many-body quantum magnet, or merely provide a skeleton of spectral weight left by the noninteracting picture, remains unclear. We study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet on the edge-centered honeycomb lattice to examine this question. In contrast to flat bands in geometrically frustrated magnets such as kagome, this lattice has a 2:3 sublattice imbalance that renders the intersublattice coupling matrix rectangular, whose null space gives rise to a flat band at the single-particle level. The same imbalance stabilizes a ferrimagnetic ground state through the Lieb--Mattis theorem and leads to an edge-site-localized flat magnon in linear spin-wave theory. Combining linear spin-wave theory, sign-problem-free stochastic series expansion quantum Monte Carlo, and stochastic analytic continuation, we find that quantum fluctuations transform this harmonic flat mode into a broad continuum whose centroid is about 1.55J and nearly dispersionless along the high-symmetry path. Sublattice imbalance thus offers an unfrustrated route that unifies flat bands and ferrimagnetism, and suggests that flat-band geometry organizes many-body spectral weight rather than giving rise to a protected quasiparticle.

papers.title_en: Krylov complexity and oscillatory quantum dynamics in two-field inflation
papers.abstract_en: We investigate Krylov-space dynamics of primordial perturbations in two-field inflation. Starting from the quadratic action for coupled curvature and entropy perturbations, we solve the mode equations with Bunch-Davies initial conditions and construct the corresponding quadratic Hamiltonian. The Gaussian quantum state is described by a four-mode squeezed state with two squeezing channels. We derive the evolution of the squeezing strength and squeezing angle and use them to evaluate the Krylov complexity, Krylov entropy, and channel-resolved Lanczos coefficients. Our numerical results show that the two channels remain weakly squeezed inside the horizon but develop different squeezing histories after horizon exit. The two channels exhibit different onset times and distinct oscillatory Krylov dynamics. The second channel develops strong squeezing earlier and dominates the intermediate evolution, whereas the first channel shows a delayed enhancement. The corresponding Krylov complexities exhibit oscillatory structures across horizon crossing and pronounced fluctuations in the strongly squeezed superhorizon regime. These oscillations originate from the relative phases entering the squeezing equations and are amplified through the nonlinear relation between Krylov complexity of different channels.

papers.title_en: Fluctuation-Induced Supersolidity at the Superfluid-Solid Interface
papers.abstract_en: Supersolidity, combining superfluid and crystalline orders, has been realized in dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates by tuning interatomic interactions. Here we show that supersolidity can also emerge from mode coupling at a superfluid-solid interface, without modifying bulk interactions and for a broad class of superfluids. Using an analytical and numerical treatment of the coupled superfluid and phonon fields, we derive the criterion for a density-modulation instability driven by interfacial coupling and dependent on dimensionality. In superfluid helium, the instability first appears at the roton mode, while in a Bose-Einstein condensate with contact interactions it occurs at the lowest accessible wave vector set by the system size. Beyond the threshold, the ground state acquires an interfacial density modulation while the bulk remains superfluid, forming a hybrid superfluid-supersolid phase. Our results identify interfacial mode coupling as a promising route to supersolidity, enabling the simultaneous exploitation of interfacial supersolid and bulk superfluid quantum properties.

papers.title_en: Numerical simulations of low-mass black hole-neutron star mergers with moderate eccentricities
papers.abstract_en: A confident detection of orbital eccentricity in gravitational-wave signals from black hole-neutron star systems would be a strong indicator of their dynamical formation origin. While eccentric waveform models have recently been developed, their validity for analyzing black hole--neutron star signals has yet to be tested against numerical-relativity simulations. Building upon our previous study of quasicircular black hole--neutron star mergers, we perform simulations of a subset of these systems with orbital eccentricities around five times larger than those inferred for GW200105_162426. Additionally, we perform simulations with magnetized matter to assess whether trapped $g$-mode oscillations persist in strongly magnetized disks. Regarding the emitted gravitational-wave signal, we find that the effective one-body waveform model SEOBNRv5EHM shows reasonable agreement unless tidal contributions become important, and the inspiral-only post-Newtonian models pyEFPE/pyEFPEHM show larger disagreement in the late inspiral. For the equal-mass system, which has the largest effective tidal deformability, eccentric tidal corrections have a small but noticeable impact on the phase, $\sim0.1$ rad. We find an almost negligible impact of eccentricity on the properties of the remnant black hole, and differences of up to a factor of two in the remnant disk mass. Trapped $g$ modes in the accretion disks have the same frequency regardless of the eccentricity, confirming that they depend mainly on the properties of the remnant black hole. We find that when accretion disks are strongly magnetized, they become less dense and have less pronounced structure, and that the trapped $g$ modes previously identified in the unmagnetized cases are efficiently damped.

papers.title_en: Double-weak-link interferometer of hard-core bosons in one dimension
papers.abstract_en: We study the dynamics of a lattice hard-core boson gas released from a domain wall initial state in the presence of two weak links (defects). When the two defects are separated by a finite distance, the resulting density profile exhibits interferences, while when we take the large-distance limit between the two defects, those interferences are averaged out and one recovers a profile that is described by the standard Euler-scale hydrodynamic description of the gas. We analyze this in detail by computing the exact fermionic propagators and their repeated reflections at the defects. We derive a closed analytic expression for the density profile during the expansion, explicitly highlighting the role played by these interference processes.
papers.journal_ref: Attila Takács et al J. Stat. Mech. (2026) 103102

papers.title_en: Quadrupole and quadratic-in-spin effects in quasicircular, spinning, asymmetric binaries
papers.abstract_en: Next-generation gravitational-wave detectors will require significant improvements in current theoretical waveform models, particularly in the case of asymmetric-mass binaries. Here we provide one such improvement by calculating fully relativistic finite-size effects for small mass ratios -- primarily, fluxes of energy -- including quadratic-in-secondary-spin terms, spin-induced quadrupole terms, and tidally induced quadrupole terms, for quasicircular inspirals of a small companion into a Kerr black hole. We formulate these calculations within a multiscale waveform-generation framework in self-force theory, which could be used, with an energy-balance law we derive, to develop self-contained waveform models for asymmetric binaries involving stars orbiting black holes. Our results could additionally be used to improve other families of waveform models across all mass ratios. We present results both as complete numerical data sets on a Chebyshev grid and as analytical post-Newtonian expansions (to sixth PN order relative to the leading term in each contribution to the flux).

papers.title_en: Quantum Cosmology in Page-Wootters' Framework: Singularity Resolution and Clock Coherence
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the fate of big-bang singularity and coherence between distinct clock states in a quantum cosmological setting within the Page-Wootters framework. With a canonically quantized plane-symmetric Bianchi I universe, we employ Dirac factorization of the Wheeler-DeWitt constraint and obtain a Schrodinger-like equation which is first-order in an internal clock variable. By constructing its solution as a Gaussian wave packet in the expanding branch, we derive the corresponding conditional state and probability density of the universe. We find that the conditional probability density vanishes in the zero-volume limit, indicating resolution of the big-bang singularity within this probabilistic framework. Another prespective of the study is provided by the construction of density matrix from the conditional states associated with different clock readings and the remaining degree of freedom. By tracing out the remaining subsystem, we obtain the reduced density matrix and analyze the resulting coherence as a function of separation between different clock states. These results provide a relational characterization of singularity resolution and demonstrate how the spectral properties of the quantum state govern the temporal coherence between different clock states in the Page-Wootters description.

papers.title_en: Non-equilibrium Muon Dynamics Imitating Fractional Spin Excitations in a Quantum Spin Chain
papers.abstract_en: Fractional spin excitations in low-dimensional and frustrated magnets are commonly associated with sporadic spin fluctuations, as observed in quantum spin liquids, spin ices, and other complex magnetic states. In this study, we investigate the spin dynamics in the amplitude-modulated magnetic ground state of AgCuVO$_4$, a spin-1/2 chain compound with competing intrachain interactions, by muon spectroscopy. Our data reveal a Gaussian decay of muon polarization that remains remarkably resilient against applied magnetic fields---a behavior often interpreted as evidence of emergent sporadic spin dynamics. However, density functional theory calculations of muon stopping sites and their quadrupolar level-crossing resonance spectra suggest an alternative mechanism: a two-state model where the muon randomly hops between two nearby sites, eventually equilibrating across both on a microsecond timescale via quantum delocalization. These findings provide a microscopic explanation for the field-resilient muon polarization and indicate that such behavior may not always stem from intrinsic spin fluctuations, but can also arise from non-equilibrium muon dynamics.

papers.title_en: Polarization Properties of Thomson-Scattering Triaxial Ellipsoids
papers.abstract_en: Polarimetry is a powerful tool for constraining the geometry of distant astrophysical objects. Continuum polarization induced by Thomson scattering can probe the photospheric geometry of transients and provide insight into their explosion mechanisms. We systematically study continuum polarization from spheroids over a broader range of deformations and viewing angles than considered previously, and generalize the calculation to triaxial ellipsoids. We find that strongly deformed spheroids exhibit a non-monotonic dependence of polarization on viewing angle, a behavior overlooked in previous studies. Triaxial ellipsoids show more diverse polarization signatures, but their qualitative behavior can be understood from the area of surface elements viewed nearly edge-on, where the local polarization is strongest. Our results provide a simple physical understanding of the dependence of polarization on photospheric geometry and help constrain the geometry of astrophysical transients through polarimetric observations. The computational results of this study will be made publicly available for use in future research.

papers.title_en: Identification of ultra-high-energy neutrinos in vertical air showers with surface detectors
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the potential of surface detector arrays to identify ultra-high-energy neutrinos using vertical air showers with zenith angle $θ\leq 60^\circ$, a region largely unexplored in current searches. The method exploits the enhanced electromagnetic component at ground level arising from energetic leptons produced in neutrino interactions. Using detailed air-shower and detector simulations, we show that observables sensitive to the electromagnetic and muonic content provide genuine discrimination between neutrino-induced and hadron-induced showers. This is demonstrated both with idealized shower quantities and with realistic detector-level signals based on water-Cherenkov and scintillator detectors. The corresponding neutrino identification efficiency is used to derive the effective mass and, primarily, the effective area of the array under background-rejection requirements appropriate to targeted multi-messenger searches. Although not competitive with inclined-shower searches under the stringent background rejection factors required for diffuse-flux analyses, this approach establishes the feasibility of a vertical detection channel, extending the field of view of surface arrays and providing a complementary tool for multi-messenger observations of transient sources.

papers.title_en: Classical conformal invariance and superhorizon dynamics in de Sitter
papers.abstract_en: Soft de Sitter Effective Theory is a well-motivated candidate for the correct effective late-time description of equal-time correlation functions in de Sitter space. In this work, we study its application to theories that enjoy classical conformal invariance, using the conformally-coupled $φ^4$-theory as a toy model. While quantum effects generate non-trivial late-time dynamics in such models, we argue that it is not described by the standard construction of the effective theory as discussed thus far in the literature. We show that the tree-level matching of the trispectrum onto the effective theory does not fit into the expected power-counting scheme, and we contrast it with the matching of the tree-level bispectrum in the conformally-coupled $φ^3$-theory, where it works consistently. We then propose a prescription to identify the leading superhorizon degrees of freedom in such theories, which should serve as the starting point for the construction of their late-time effective description. The interpretation of logarithms of the form $\log(-kη)$ in this context is briefly discussed.

papers.title_en: Difference between pair creation and anomaly matching: Nontrivial aspects of invertible symmetries and defects in $SU(N)$ models
papers.abstract_en: We study the connection between the $SU(N)_{K}$ Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model and $SU(N)_{K'}$ WZW models, enforcing the unbroken $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ symmetries. The fundamental underlying structures are the (half-)integer spin simple currents in the topological quantum field theories and anomaly matching conditions in conformal field theories. For the (half-)integer spin simple current condition of the folded models $SU(N)_{K}\boxtimes_{\mathbb{Z}_{N}} \overline{SU(N)_{K'}}$ or $SU(N)_{K}\boxtimes_{\mathbb{Z}_{N}} SU(N)_{K'}$, we obtain the generalized pairing condition $K= \pm R^{2}K' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=1$. On the other hand, the anomaly matching condition results in the weaker condition $K= \pm RUK' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=\text{gcd}(U,N)=1$. Surprisingly, the anomaly matching without the pairing condition results in the intrinsic mismatch of the preservation law of the $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ defects and symmetries. The pairing condition canonically relates symmetries and defects, as in category theory, whereas it is unclear whether it can be a guiding principle in prohibiting the massless renormalization group flows.

papers.title_en: Resolving the Assembly of Disk Galaxies from the Epoch of Reionisation to Cosmic Noon
papers.abstract_en: Most of the mass and angular momentum of today's disk galaxies assembled at $z>1$. Yet, it remains unclear how these galaxies acquired their gas, how their baryons and dark matter coevolved, and how feedback and radial gas transport shaped their disks. Addressing these gaps requires resolved observations of cold gas, which carries most of the mass and angular momentum involved in galaxy assembly. By resolving CO and [C II] at kpc scales, ALMA revealed a surprising population of rotation-dominated disks, even at $z>2$, exhibiting kinematic signatures consistent with spiral arms, bars, and tidal tails. Yet, these studies are limited to massive ($M_\star>10^{10.5}$ M$_\odot$) and highly star-forming (SFRs$\gtrsim 100$ M$_\odot$yr$^{-1}$) galaxies, the progenitors of today's most massive elliptical and disk galaxies. To understand how most present-day spirals (like the Milky Way) assembled, it is crucial to resolve their low-mass progenitors, which dominate the star-forming galaxy population by number at $z>1$. Achieving this goal demands a tenfold increase in line sensitivity and hence a next-generation sub-/millimetre facility: ALMA2040. This leap in sensitivity will enable routine resolved studies of hundreds of $M_\star>10^9$ M$_\odot$ galaxies, including those on and below the main sequence of star-forming galaxies, providing representative, statistical galaxy samples with sub-kpc constraints on the cold gas kinematics and morphology. By uniquely providing resolved CO, [C I], and [C II] observations across $z=1-6$, ALMA2040 will trace a much larger fraction of the cold-gas reservoir than is accessible today, extending resolved studies from rare massive and/or lensed systems to representative galaxy populations. In this way, ALMA2040 will transform our understanding of how galaxy disks formed and evolved.

papers.title_en: Bound States Inside the Horizon and Black Hole Entropy
papers.abstract_en: We study the bound states perturbations in the interior of the Schwarzschild black hole and examine whether or not their microstates spectrum can furnish a statistical description of the black hole entropy. These states contain a discrete set of modes characterized by the labels $(s, p,\ell,m)$, where $s$ represents the spin of the species, $p$ denotes the radial excitation number while $(\ell,m)$ are the usual angular momentum labels. Requiring that the shortest wavelength resolved by the highly excited bound states remains above the quantum gravity scale introduces an angular cutoff $\ell_{\rm max}\sim r_H/L_{\rm Pl}$. The resulting angular degeneracy therefore scales with the horizon area. We count the corresponding configurations in the microcanonical ensemble and find an entropy of the form $S_{\rm bs}=αA/\hbar G$. Demanding that the bound state sector to be in thermal equilibrium with the black hole at the Hawking temperature fixes the fraction of the bound state energy in total black hole energy. For the gravitational perturbations sector, the equilibrium bound state contribution in entropy and the energy fraction are typically small. We also examine the conditions under which the bound states could account for the full black hole entropy. Although such saturation is possible at the level of state counting, it requires an order unity fraction in the black hole energy and therefore the backreactions on the background geometry cannot be ignored.

papers.title_en: Extended parameterized spin expansion formalism for ringdown analysis with GW250114
papers.abstract_en: Parameterized descriptions of black-hole quasinormal-mode spectra are essential for testing gravity with ringdown observations. We extend the Parameterized Spin Expansion Coefficients (ParSpec) formalism by simultaneously sampling the characteristic length scale $\tilde{\ell}$ and the scaling index $\tilde{p}$, rather than fixing $\tilde{p}$ to a theory-motivated integer and constraining $\tilde{\ell}$. Physically, this extension promotes the scaling of the spectral corrections coming from higher-curvature operators to an observable quantity. Methodologically, it enables us to investigate the enlarged ParSpec parameter space and identify the prior geometry induced by conditions on the effective coupling $γ$. We examine the robustness of the framework by using the $220$ and $220+221$ ringdown models over different start times with informative priors on mass and luminosity for GW250114, and further study a joint constraint with GW231123. We pointed out that $γ<1$ avoids an artificial correlation between $\tilde{p}$ and $\tilde{\ell}$ among the coupling prescriptions considered, and the choices of ringdown starting time and QNM mode content in the ParSpec framework should be matched to the information content and resolving power of the data. Higher-SNR ringdowns and hierarchical analyses of a larger event population will be required to break the $\tilde{p}$-$\tilde{\ell}$ degeneracy and directly probe the scaling structure of corrections to GR.

papers.title_en: Loop Quantum Kaluza-Klein Cosmology and Inflation
papers.abstract_en: We present the detailed analyses of five-dimensional loop quantum Kaluza-Klein cosmology based on the symmetric reduction of the connection formulation of the full theory. The previous results in a particular scenario are extended to more general cases. The effective scalar constraint for the geometric sector of the model is derived by the systematic semi-classical analysis in both the canonical and path-integral formulations, incorporating the quantum fluctuations as a subleading-order correction. The resulting effective scalar constraint not only exhibits the correct classical limit of the quantum system, but also serves as the basis for investigating the following three distinct effective scenarios through the incorporation of matter contributions: (i) vacuum, (ii) minimally coupling with a scalar field, and (iii) coupling with the dust. In all the three effective scenarios, the big bang and potential past big rip singularities in the classical model are naturally resolved by including the leading-order quantum correction of holonomies. Moreover, the visible universe undergoes a super-inflationary phase after overcoming the classical big bang singularity, during which the phenomenologically desired 55 e-folds can be achieved by appropriate initial conditions. In the case where the subleading-order quantum fluctuation term is included as a constant, the evolutions of the five-dimensional universe in all the three effective scenarios not only achieve sufficient inflation in the visible dimensions, but also exhibit re-collapse behaviors at certain large scales. Hence the cosmic inflation may originate from the interplay between compact extra dimensions and quantum geometric effects.

papers.title_en: Pairing-channel reconstruction by Ising spin-orbit coupling in a multiorbital triangular-lattice model
papers.abstract_en: Ising spin-orbit coupling (SOC) is widely known for locking electronic spins and protecting superconductivity against in-plane paramagnetic pair breaking. Here we show that, in a correlated multiorbital system, Ising SOC can play a qualitatively different role: it reconstructs the hierarchy of spin-fluctuation-mediated pairing channels by reshaping the low-energy Fermi surfaces, orbital-spin coherence factors, and momentum-resolved scattering phase space. We study a noncentrosymmetric two-orbital triangular-lattice model with Rashba SOC, Ising SOC, and onsite SOC. We solve the pairing problem within a multiorbital random-phase-approximation framework. In the single-orbital limit, an $E$-representation state with a dominant $S_z=0$ component emerges only at relatively strong Ising SOC. Orbital degrees of freedom facilitate the stabilization of this pairing state at a smaller nominal Ising SOC strength and generate a broad competition between $E$ and $A_1$ pairing channels. The $E$ state can maintain the same $S_z=0$ triplet character, whereas the $A_1$ state becomes a fully gapped sign-changing $\splusminus$ superconductor. The latter also realizes a topologically nontrivial phase in the time-reversal-invariant weak-pairing regime, with a nonzero $\mathbb{Z}_2$ index, Wilson-loop spectral flow, and boundary modes. Its topology is not carried by a single orbital pairing component, but emerges cooperatively from the dominant intra- and inter-orbital pairing components. These results establish a microscopic route by which Ising SOC and orbital hybridization can reconstruct interaction-driven superconductivity, producing both Ising-triplet and topological singlet-dominated phases in correlated non-centrosymmetric systems.

papers.title_en: Electrically charged regular black holes in higher dimensions: Maxwellian limit, branch point of the Lagrangian, and thermodynamics
papers.abstract_en: Electrically charged regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics are known to require a double-valued Lagrangian density $L(F)$, with a branch point at the radius where the electromagnetic invariant attains its extremum. We extend the construction of such black holes to an arbitrary number of spacetime dimensions $D\geq4$ and obtain a new family of solutions that unifies the Bardeen and Hayward black holes in a single analytic form, with a single nonlinearity parameter $γ$. We show that the Maxwellian weak-field limit is recovered if and only if $γ=D-3$, so that the Bardeen and Hayward black holes, which lack this limit in four dimensions, become Maxwellian in five and six dimensions, respectively. The matter sector is written in the dual $P$ framework as a Hamiltonian density $H(P)$ that contains only fixed coupling constants, so that the mass and the charge of the black hole appear as integration constants of a fixed theory; the regular solutions form a one-parameter subfamily in which the mass is tied to the charge. We locate the branch point of $Ł(F)$ in closed form and find that it is always hidden inside the event horizon in four dimensions, whereas for $D\geq5$ it emerges from the horizon for near-extremal charges and becomes visible to a distant observer. The null and weak energy conditions are satisfied everywhere, the strong energy condition is violated only inside the horizon, and the dominant energy condition is violated at large distances only for $γ>D-3$. Finally, since the theory is fixed, the first law of black hole thermodynamics holds in its standard form; we derive the horizon potential in closed form, the extended first law with the couplings as thermodynamic variables, and the corresponding Smarr formula.

papers.title_en: Axial gravitational quasinormal modes of magnetically charged black holes
papers.abstract_en: In this paper, we consider axial perturbations on the magnetically charged string-inspired Euler-Heisenberg black hole. Since axial metric perturbation decouples from axial electromagnetic perturbation, here we mainly focus on axial gravitational perturbation. By using WKB approximation and AIM methods, we make a detailed analysis of the gravitational quasinormal frequencies by varying the characteristic parameters of gravitational perturbation and black holes. It is found these results obtained through the AIM method are in good agreement with those of obtained by WKB method, including these results extracted from the time-domain profiles. The greybody factor is calculated by WKB method. The effects of these parameters $Q_m$, $ε$ and multipole number $l$ on the greybody factor are also studied.

papers.title_en: Mock Catalogs of Strongly Lensed Gravitational Waves via a Halo Model Approach with Space-borne Detectors
papers.abstract_en: Future space-borne gravitational-wave (GW) detectors, such as LISA and DECIGO, are expected to detect a large number of GW events, a fraction of which may be strongly lensed by intervening galaxies or galaxy clusters. In this work, we develop a comprehensive framework to simulate strongly lensed GWs in the context of space-borne detectors. Based on realistic astrophysical models for both the source population and the lens distribution, we construct mock catalogs of lensed GW events, referred to as \textbf{GW-LMC-Space}. Our results show that, for a four-year LISA observation, the expected number of lensed events ranges from $0$ to $131$, depending on the adopted formation model of massive black hole binaries (MBHBs). The corresponding lensing probability for MBHBs can reach up to $\sim 0.3\%$. For DECIGO, we find that the number of lensed events in a one-year observation is expected to lie in the range of $0$--$44$, with a lensing probability of $\sim 0.15\%$ for stellar-mass binary black holes (BBHs), binary neutron stars (BNSs), and neutron star--black hole binaries (NSBHs). We further show that the overlap of lensed signals is a common feature in space-borne detectors, which can significantly affect both the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) estimation and event identification. These results highlight the importance of accounting for signal overlap in the analysis of strongly lensed GW events in future space-borne GW observations.

papers.title_en: Thermodynamic-limit bootstrap: Solving fractional quantum Hall ground states
papers.abstract_en: Strongly interacting ground states are usually computed in finite systems and then extrapolated to the thermodynamic limit (TDL). Here we develop a quantum many-body bootstrap that solves fractional quantum Hall ground states directly in the TDL. The method gives rigorous and quantitatively tight lower bounds on the ground-state energy and identifies the ground-state structure and topological order. For Laughlin and Pfaffian parent Hamiltonians, it reproduces exact pair-correlation functions and low-lying orbital entanglement spectrum (OES) nearly level by level. For Coulomb interactions, the rigorous TDL energy bounds closely match thermodynamic estimates from exact diagonalization and density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) extrapolations, and the local diagnostics recover established Laughlin and Moore--Read OES counting and Friedel oscillations of the composite Fermi liquid. Beyond these benchmarks, the bootstrap resolves the thermodynamic ground states at $ν=1/4$ and $ν=12/5$, identifying a composite Fermi liquid and $\overline{\mathrm{RR}}_3$ topological order, respectively. The same framework applies equally well to Abelian and non-Abelian, gapped and gapless quantum Hall states. The TDL bootstrap therefore provides a general ground-state solver that determines both the energy and the state directly in the TDL.

papers.title_en: Analytical solutions for timelike orbits around Damour-Solodukhin wormholes
papers.abstract_en: We investigate timelike geodesics around Damour-Solodukhin wormholes, which are Schwarzschild-like geometries characterized by a deformation parameter $λ$ that determines the radius of the throat, $r_{\rm th}$. The radial potential admits four roots, including the throat radius itself, allowing the throat to merge with other roots and form double, triple, and quartic degeneracies. Triple-root configurations associated with the throat, in principle, can determine the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), which provides a potential observational distinction from Schwarzschild black holes. Using the Mino-time parametrization, we derive particle trajectories with closed-form analytical solutions in terms of incomplete elliptic integrals for both bound and unbound motion. Our focus is on the location of double or triple roots at the throat, where the azimuthal angle and coordinate time of orbital motion show logarithmic or power-law divergence as the particle approaches the throat. By contrast, trajectories remain regular when the throat corresponds to a simple root, allowing particles to traverse smoothly between the two asymptotically flat regions. We also derive exact homoclinic solutions associated with the throat and compute the corresponding Lyapunov exponent. In addition, inspiral and plunge trajectories through the throat are analyzed. These results provide analytic insights into the particle dynamics and possible observational signatures of the wormholes.

papers.title_en: Transdimensional Chern insulators in rhombohedral multilayer graphene superlattices
papers.abstract_en: Recent experiments on lightly electron-doped rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) in the "transdimensional" regime revealed anomalous Hall hysteresis under both perpendicular and in-plane magnetic fields, pointing to the emergence of transdimensional orbital magnetism in an interaction-driven "Fermi-lune" metal. Here we demonstrate that, by coupling to the moiré potential, this transdimensional orbital ferromagnetic metal can evolve into quantized Chern insulator phases in twisted RMG/hBN moiré superlattices. Using unrestricted Hartree-Fock calculations, we find that interaction-driven reconstruction isolates a spin-valley-polarized $|C| = 1$ Chern band, leading to a "transdimensional Chern insulator" (TDCI) state exhibiting both in-plane and out-of-plane orbital magnetizations. A minimal two-band model is introduced to describe the unique properties of TDCI, which unveils the intimate connection between non-reciprocal velocity and in-plane orbital magnetization. We further analyze the collective excitations of TDCIs, and identify soft charge and spin modes that may lead to density wave instabilities in certain cases. An in-plane magnetic field can harden the soft density-wave mode and may drive a transition from density-wave state to TDCI. Finally, when the $|C| = 1$ band is fractionally filled, the many-body ground state may be a fractional Chern insulator with broken rotation and mirror symmetries.

papers.title_en: A GLSM realization of derived equivalence in $U(1) \times U(2)$ models
papers.abstract_en: This paper studies the derived equivalence between Calabi--Yau mixed branches using the B-brane hemisphere partition function in anomalous gauged linear sigma models (GLSMs). For a family of anomalous $U(2)$ GLSMs, we study the infrared behavior of B-branes under RG flow and the variation of FI parameters in the quantum Kähler moduli space. As characterized by the big and small window categories of the GLSM, the RG flow effect is analyzed according to the properties of their B-brane central charges as hemisphere partition functions. The result generalizes the band restriction rules in anomalous abelian GLSMs (Clingempeel--Floch--Romo) to some $U(2)$ models. As an application, we study a family of $U(1)\times U(k)$ models for $k=1,2$, which realize a Fano UV sigma model and two IR phases as mixed branches accompanied by local Calabi--Yau Higgs components. By applying the restriction rules, we establish new derived equivalences between Calabi--Yau varieties from these anomalous models.

papers.title_en: Unique Charge-density-wave Order and Fluctuation-induced Phonon Softening in the Optimally-doped Trilayer Cuprate Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{10+δ}$
papers.abstract_en: Charge-density-wave (CDW) order is a ubiquitous feature of cuprate superconductors that competes with superconductivity. However, its behavior remains poorly understood in trilayer compounds, which contain the optimal number of CuO$_2$ layers for superconductivity. Here, we report Cu $L_3$- and O $K$-edge resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) measurements of optimally-doped Bi$_{2}$Sr$_{2}$Ca$_{2}$Cu$_{3}$O$_{10+δ}$ (Bi2223), the trilayer cuprate with the highest superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) among Bi-based cuprates. We observe CDW order with a single in-plane wavevector of ${\bm q}_{\text{CDW}} = (0.25, 0)$, demonstrating that a coherent CDW order is formed across the trilayers. We also resolve CDW fluctuations emanating from the static order, whose profiles differ between the Cu $L_3$ and O $K$ edges. The phonon softening occurs where these CDW fluctuations interact with the phonon branch, indicating that the RIXS phonon anomaly is driven by the coupling between CDW fluctuations and the phonon branch.

papers.title_en: Quantum Many-Body Mpemba Effect through Ruelle-Pollicott Resonances
papers.abstract_en: Relaxation towards equilibrium is often assumed to be slower when a system starts farther from equilibrium, but this intuition fails in the Mpemba effect. Recent advances in controllable quantum platforms have enabled the exploration of its quantum analogue, the quantum Mpemba effect (QME), yet its microscopic origin remains largely unclear. Here we provide a general framework for understanding the QME in closed quantum many-body chaotic systems by reformulating the equilibration process of local subsystems in terms of Ruelle-Pollicott (RP) resonances. We show that suppressing the initial-state overlap with the dominant RP resonant mode accelerates subsystem equilibration and thereby yields the QME. We further uncover that a novel type of strong QME can occur via complete translation-symmetry breaking of initial states. We substantiate our predictions using the prototypical kicked Ising chain and a quantum automaton circuit. These findings cast the QME in closed many-body systems into a unified framework with open-system analogues and provide experimentally accessible signatures on state-of-the-art quantum platforms.

papers.title_en: Optical observations of supernova candidates with the ILMT
papers.abstract_en: The International Liquid Mirror Telescope (ILMT) is a 4-m optical ({\em gri} spectral bands) zenithal survey telescope with a field of view of 22.3$\times$22.3 arcmin, suitable for discovery and follow-up of faint transients. With the \texttt{PyLMT} pipeline, several new transients, including supernova candidates, are being discovered and detected routinely. We report the discovery of six supernova candidates, AT~2023yjc, AT~2024agkc, AT~2024aifv, AT~2024aiha, AT~2024fxn, and AT~2024zsm, using the ILMT. Ten additional supernova candidates were discovered in other surveys but were also detected with the ILMT. Here, we present the light curves of all supernova candidates observed with the ILMT in the {\em gri} bands. The basic light curve parameters, such as the rise time, decline rate, and peak magnitude, are estimated and reported.

papers.title_en: Model-independent parameters from DESI DR1 LRG2 with an explicitly varying power-spectrum shape
papers.abstract_en: Distinguishing between dark energy and modified gravity as the origin of the accelerated expansion requires the cosmic distances and the growth of structure to be measured in a model-independent way. Such measurements are difficult to perform while the primordial shape parameters are varied at the same time, and those parameters are therefore usually held fixed at the values determined by cosmic microwave background experiments. In this work, we present a methodology that constrains the shape parameters simultaneously with the model-independent distance and growth parameters, using an emulator built upon a hybrid model in which perturbative predictions are supplemented by templates measured from $N$-body simulations. {Because these templates are measured rather than expanded, the model carries non-linear corrections beyond the order at which its perturbative part is truncated, so that its accuracy on small scales is set by the simulations rather than by the reach of the expansion.} A Gaussian process emulator supplies these templates rapidly across the space of scale-dependent parameters, which makes the joint analysis computationally feasible, and the emulator is trained and validated over a range spanning $5σ$ of the Planck constraints. Applying the method to the LRG2 sample of DESI DR1, we obtain measurements of the Alcock--Paczynski parameters $α_\perp$ and $α_{||}$ and of the growth rate $fσ_8$. {With the tight Planck prior adopted here the constraints differ from those obtained with the shape parameters held fixed by less than a twentieth of their own uncertainties, so that the choice of template contributes at that level to the error budget of the measurement. Projected onto flat $Λ$CDM after the fit, the three measurements are mutually consistent, with $χ^2=0.7$ for two degrees of freedom, and require $h=0.724\pm0.017$.

papers.title_en: Plasmon Collapse in a Directional Strange Metal
papers.abstract_en: Strange metals are widespread in strongly correlated quantum matter and closely intertwined with high-temperature superconductivity and quantum criticality, yet their microscopic charge dynamics remain fundamentally unresolved. Whether well-defined collective modes survive in an incoherent electronic fluid or dissolve into overdamped continua remains intensely debated. Here, employing high-momentum-resolution inelastic electron scattering complemented by direction-resolved transport, we show that the van der Waals compound $\mathrm{MoOCl}_2$, a "bad" metal known to host unusually "good" plasmons, exhibits a striking dichotomy in electronic coherence and charge dynamics. Transport reveals coherent Fermi liquid behavior along one in-plane crystallographic axis and an incoherent strange metal response along the orthogonal axis. This dichotomy extends directly to the charge response. The Fermi liquid direction supports a well-defined, long-lived plasmon, whereas the strange metal direction exhibits an overdamped excitation that progressively loses its collective character with increasing momentum. Beyond a critical momentum ($q_c$ $\approx$ 0.008 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}^{-1}$), the mode undergoes a reversal into negative dispersion and ultimately collapses into a broad, nearly featureless continuum with a robust high-energy boundary ($E_c$ $\approx$ 1.75 eV). Remarkably, thickness-dependent measurements show that both $q_c$ and $E_c$ remain nearly unchanged despite substantial modifications of Coulomb screening, revealing them as intrinsic scales of incoherent charge density fluctuations. These results establish a unique single-material platform in which coherent and incoherent electronic states are partitioned into in-plane orthogonal channels, and demonstrate that incoherent electronic fluids retain intrinsically structured charge dynamics beyond the quasiparticle paradigm.

papers.title_en: Gauging Modulated Symmetries: Bond Algebras, Higher-Form Symmetries, and Symmetry-Enriched Topological Order
papers.abstract_en: We develop a constructive framework for characterizing modulated symmetries and their gauging in $d$-dimensional lattice systems. The modulation profiles are organized as a finite-dimensional representation of the space group acting on a finite Abelian internal symmetry group. Since the corresponding automorphism group is finite, the nontrivial spatial action factors through a finite quotient of the space group, leading to periodic modulation patterns and providing a classification framework for discrete Abelian modulated symmetries. The symmetry-allowed local interactions are systematically obtained from a kernel construction, which also yields an algebra of open operators. Upon gauging, its elements are transmuted into extended Wilson and boundary operators while retaining their algebraic relations. In the deconfined regime, the resulting algebra realizes a mixed 't Hooft anomaly, providing a microscopic route to Abelian crystalline symmetry-enriched topological phases (SETs). These SETs do not mix electric and magnetic sectors, which transform in mutually contragredient representations, thereby preserving their braiding pairing. We illustrate the framework through explicit examples and show that several models present in the literature fit naturally within our construction.

papers.title_en: Dark Matter Particle Explorer: Ten-Year On-Orbit Performance and Scientific Outcomes
papers.abstract_en: The Dark Matter Particle Explorer (DAMPE, also known as ``Wukong'') is the first scientific space mission within the framework of the Strategic Pioneer Program on Space Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The main scientific objectives of DAMPE include indirect detection of dark matter, cosmic-ray physics, and high energy gamma-ray astronomy. Thanks to its large geometrical factor and thick imaging calorimeter, DAMPE could effectively detect cosmic-ray electrons (including positrons) and gamma-rays up to 10~TeV, and nuclei up to PeV. Since launched on 17 December 2015 into a Sun-synchronous orbit, DAMPE has been smoothly operating on orbit for more than ten years. Here we present an overview of instrument, on-orbit status, and highlight scientific results of DAMPE, including the measurements of the all-electron energy spectrum and the spectra of protons and other nuclei, and high energy gamma-ray line search.

papers.title_en: Strain-enhanced superconductivity in RuO$_2$ thin films: Joint experimental and theoretical studies
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the superconducting properties of RuO$_2$ films grown on TiO$_2$ substrates by combining film fabrication and transport measurement with \textit{ab initio} calculation. Experimentally, we grow several RuO$_2$ (110) thin films on TiO$_2$ (110) substrates and observe superconductivity with critical temperature ($T_c$) of $\sim$2.0 K in 20-nm and 30-nm RuO$_2$ (110) thin films. Theoretically, we study the superconductivity in both RuO$_2$ (110) and RuO$_2$ (100) epitaxial films within McMillan formalism of isotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory. Among the salient results, the calculated phonon dispersion relations of all the considered RuO$_2$ films show that the epitaxial films are dynamically stable. Importantly, our \textit{ab initio} calculations reveal that independent of the film orientation, the [001] compressive strain $ε_{[001]}$ pushes the flat Ru $d_{z^2}$-dominant bands towards the Fermi level ($E_F$), and significantly soften the out-of-plane acoustic phonon mode near the R point in the Brillouin zone, which substantially enhances the electron-phonon coupling (EPC) strength $λ$ and hence the calculated $T_c$ in the RuO$_2$ films. Remarkably, the amount of the phonon softening and the enhanced $T_c$ increase almost linearly with the increasing $ε_{[001]}$. The calculated $T_c$ for the films with thickness of $\geq$ 20 nm agree well with the experimental $T_c$. These findings demonstrate that among other things, lattice mismatch strain provides an effective route for tuning phonon-mediated superconductivity in RuO$_2$ and other thin films.

papers.title_en: Linear causality and stability constraints on relativistic second-order magnetohydrodynamics
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we construct a theoretical framework for relativistic second-order magnetohydrodynamics based on entropy current analysis. The formalism consistently incorporates finite relaxation dynamics of the dissipative fluxes, providing a transient framework suitable for analyzing linear stability and short-wavelength causality. Utilizing linear mode analysis, we investigate the constraints imposed by causality and stability on this anisotropic system. By linearizing the theory around a homogeneous equilibrium state, we identify the magnetosonic, Alfvén, and charge-diffusion sectors, together with their coupling terms. For each sector, we derive asymptotic dispersion relations in both the long-wavelength (small-$k$) and short-wavelength (large-$k$) regimes, validating them against exact numerical roots. Our numerical analysis confirms the accuracy of these asymptotic solutions and uncovers a nontrivial angular dependence, especially near special propagation directions where the ordinary momentum expansion becomes less reliable. By evaluating the large-$k$ behavior of the propagating branches alongside the damping properties of non-hydrodynamic modes, we delineate the corresponding causality constraints. We find that the admissible linear causal domain is governed by the interplay between propagation direction, anisotropic transport coefficients, and relaxation times, with the resulting bounds being intrinsically mode-dependent. These findings provide a systematic theoretical basis for investigating linear stability and short-wavelength causality in relativistic magnetohydrodynamics beyond the first-order approximation.

papers.title_en: Fast X-ray Transient EP260321a: Shock Breakout through an Extended Circumstellar Matter
papers.abstract_en: The Einstein Probe (EP) has discovered a fast X-ray transient, EP260321a, whose optical counterpart was subsequently classified as a broad-lined Type Ic supernova. Its observed rise time of about 690 seconds is inconsistent with theoretical predictions for shock breakout (SBO) from a Wolf-Rayet star, which is typically regarded as the progenitor of envelope-stripped supernovae. In this paper, we propose that EP260321a arose from a SBO within extended circumstellar matter (CSM), where breakout photons were initially trapped, then diffused out of the unshocked CSM as the ejecta expanded and the opacity decreased. We modeled this photon diffusion process using both Monte Carlo simulations and an analytical approach to describe the temperature evolution. Through Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling, we obtain the best-fit CSM parameters of log10(Mcsm/Msun) = -3.3 for the total CSM mass, Rin = 160 Rsun for the inner CSM radius, and Rout = 612 Rsun for the outer CSM radius. The presence of such a dense CSM indicates that the progenitor of EP260321a underwent episodic mass loss just days before the explosion, providing new observational constraints on the late-stage evolution of massive stars.

papers.title_en: Localized states of the non-Hermitian Schr{ö}dinger equation with a complex $1/r^{2}$ potential: from Efimov states to bipolarons
papers.abstract_en: We study the non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation with a complex $1/r^{2}$ potential, which bridges Hermitian few-body and non-Hermitian many-body physics: a real attractive potential describes Efimov bound states, whereas a purely imaginary one describes the medium-induced interaction between two heavy polarons at large separations. We solve this equation analytically, obtaining both the localized and continuum states, and compare the solutions with numerical and WKB results. As the imaginary part of the potential is increased, the energies of the Efimov bound states acquire imaginary parts and rotate counterclockwise in the complex plane. On approaching the purely imaginary potential, the excited states disappear sequentially, while the Efimov ground state is smoothly connected to a bipolaron state localized at short distance. Such a bipolaron is localized solely by the medium-induced imaginary interaction, without any attractive real potential. Solving the equation by finite differences, we find that each bipolaron state is necessarily accompanied by another localized state that oscillates on the scale of the mesh size and hence has no counterpart in the continuum limit. Each such pair coalesces at an exceptional point as the strength of the purely imaginary potential is varied, whereas the coalescence is lifted once a finite real part is introduced. We show that this behavior originates from a symmetry of the discretized Schrödinger equation that holds for any purely imaginary potential.

papers.title_en: Modified anisotropy and distinct phase diagrams in the nearly isotropic $S=1$ triangular-lattice antiferromagnet $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$
papers.abstract_en: The triangular-lattice antiferromagnet serves as a benchmark platform for realizing exotic quantum phases, in which magnetic anisotropy plays an essential role. In this work, we report modified magnetic anisotropy and phase diagrams in the nearly isotropic $S=1$ triangular-lattice antiferromagnet $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$, compared with those of its isostructural analog $\mathrm{K_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$. The magnetic susceptibility of $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$ exhibits an easy-axis anisotropy with $g_c > g_{ab}$, opposite to the easy-plane anisotropy observed in $\mathrm{K_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$. The single Néel transition observed at zero field splits into two transitions at around 10~T, and a magnetization plateau is observed between 21~T and 37~T for both out-of-plane ($H\parallel c$) and in-plane ($H\parallel ab$) field directions in $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$. We construct magnetic phase diagrams that are distinct between $\mathrm{Rb_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$ and $\mathrm{K_2Ni(SeO_3)_2}$. These findings highlight the sensitivity of field-induced magnetic phase behavior to anisotropy in nearly isotropic triangular-lattice antiferromagnets.

papers.title_en: A Functorial Theory of Defects in Abelian Chern-Simons Theory
papers.abstract_en: Recent work has constructed Abelian Chern-Simons theories as categorical TQFTs, allowing us to naturally incorporate categorical defects and construct defect extensions of Abelian Chern-Simons TQFTs. We first identify the Turaev-Viro realizations of Abelian Chern-Simons theory in the center and doubled pointed modular cases, clarifying the distinction between single bulk realizations and canonical doubled ones. Then we obtain Turaev-Viro partition functions in terms of Reidemeister-torsion densities. Alternatively, the Alterfold construction supplies the associated topological boundaries, domain walls, and condensation sectors, establishing an explicit Alterfold/Chern-Simons dictionary. We show that the finite quadratic module is the invariant controlling the bulk theory, its topological symmetries, orientation-reversal invariance, and defects. We further show that multicomponent Abelian BF theory arises as the extended TQFT of an off-diagonal Abelian Chern-Simons theory, placing it naturally within the same extended framework. Finally, we demonstrate that recently proposed Abelian Chern-Simons dualities do not define a genuine TQFT duality. These results provide a concrete model for defects in Abelian topological orders and suggest a route toward the non-Abelian case.

papers.title_en: Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes with NUT charge
papers.abstract_en: We construct an exact NUT-charged generalization of the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole in the Einstein-phantom-scalar system. The solution is stationary, asymptotically locally flat at both ends and free of curvature singularities. It inherits characteristic features of the Taub-NUT geometry, including the Dirac-Misner string and closed timelike curves, while the absence of Killing horizons eliminates the horizon-induced infinite winding of geodesics and renders the spacetime geodesically complete. By allowing the phantom field to have a nontrivial scalar potential with an infinite sequence of AdS vacua, we also obtain an exact asymptotically locally AdS wormhole with a NUT charge, which interpolates between different vacua at its two asymptotic ends. Using the covariant phase space formalism, we show that the Hamiltonian charges associated with the two asymptotic regions are finite under appropriate scalar boundary conditions. By performing a double Wick rotation to Euclidean signature, we demonstrate that the conformal class of the resulting metric admits an ambi-Kähler structure.

papers.title_en: Formation of Trapped Surfaces for the Einstein-Euler System
papers.abstract_en: We prove the formation of trapped surfaces for the Einstein--Euler system in 3+1 dimensions beyond spherical symmetry. We consider smooth characteristic initial data in a short-pulse regime with rapid fluid injection. Starting from initial data containing no trapped surfaces, we obtain two sufficient criteria for trapped surface formation, corresponding to the shear and fluid contributions, respectively. In particular, for the fluid-driven criterion, we impose no positive lower bound on the shear flux. To handle the multiple propagation speeds associated with gravitational waves, sound waves, and fluid transport, our analysis combines three ingredients: a coercive fluid energy current whose null fluxes reflect the unequal velocity components, curvature renormalizations adapted to the matter terms, and weighted geometric estimates controlling derivatives in all spacetime directions. To ensure that fluid injection alone can lead to trapped surface formation, we use particle-number conservation in a designed spacetime region to control the focusing process and obtain the desired sphere-integrated fluxes.

papers.title_en: Displacement-noise-free gravitational-wave detector using quantum tomography of photon orbital angular momentum states
papers.abstract_en: Gravitational waves (GWs) induce quantum transitions between photon orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) states with amplitudes $α_{\pm}$. Exploiting this effect, we present a displacement-noise-free detection framework that extracts GW information from the OAM Hilbert space. Parametrized quantum state tomography of the GW-induced OAM sidebands enables a single V-shaped detector to resolve all seven wave parameters: the frequency, propagation direction, two polarization amplitudes, and initial phase of each polarization. Direct detection of the sidebands yields a weak signal of approximately $10^{-15}\,\mathrm{W}$. We therefore introduce a stronger reference state $r |0>_{\mathrm{P}}$, with $r=0.01$, to enhance the detected signal. For an arm length of $L=4\,\mathrm{m}$, $N=160$ round trips, a paraxial parameter of $γ=0.1$, an incident light power of $P_{\mathrm{BS}}=10\,\mathrm{kW}$, a wavelength of $λ_{\mathrm{opt}}=1064\,\mathrm{nm}$, and GW amplitudes of $A=10^{-18}$, we estimate sideband transition amplitudes of $|α_{\pm}|\sim10^{-10}$ and signal powers of order $1\,\mathrm{nW}$, scaling as $P_{\mathrm{BS}}α_{\pm}\propto P_{\mathrm{BS}}ANLγ/λ_{\mathrm{opt}}$. The shot-noise-limited sensitivity floor is $S^{1/2}_n=1.6\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1/2}$. Because the scheme measures OAM transition amplitudes rather than differential arm lengths, it is intrinsically free from displacement noise and provides a broadband probe of GWs, specifically bridging the $0.1$--$10\,\mathrm{Hz}$ mid-frequency gap.

papers.title_en: Neutrino production at the extreme vicinity of supermassive black hole in NGC 1068
papers.abstract_en: The identification of NGC~1068 as an extragalactic high-energy neutrino source raises the question of the physical conditions required for neutrino production. Motivated by the newly updated IceCube data (down to $\sim 0.2 \,\rm TeV$) for NGC 1068, we present a statistical, model-independent inference primarily constrained by the multi-messenger observations. We calculate neutrino production from hadronic channels (including hadronuclear and photomeson processes) and the accompanying cascade gamma rays, and then employ the Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) method to explore the parameter space comprehensively, constrained by observational data. According to our results, the emission region is tightly limited: $R \gtrsim 10\,R_{\rm s}$ is excluded at $\sim 5σ$, and $R \gtrsim 6\,R_{\rm s}$ at $\sim 3σ$, where $R_{\rm s}$ is Schwarzschild radius of supermassive black hole (SMBH). Furthermore, reproducing $\gtrsim 80\%$ of the observed neutrino flux further restricts the emission to $R \lesssim 3R_{\rm s}$. Finally, we explore the possible particle acceleration mechanisms and find that stochastic acceleration naturally satisfies all constraints, whereas alternative mechanisms require extreme, fine-tuning parameters. We therefore identify stochastic acceleration as the most viable origin of the neutrino emission from NGC~1068.

papers.title_en: Detecting and Identifying Supernovae in AGN Accretion Disks
papers.abstract_en: Stars may become embedded in active galactic nucleus (AGN) accretion disks and eventually explode as supernovae (SNe), whose detection would provide direct evidence for the existence and evolution of stars in AGN disks. We investigate the electromagnetic emission of such disk SNe using an analytic shock dynamics model coupled with a one-zone radiation model. Applying this framework to four progenitor types over a range of AGN black hole masses and Eddington ratios, we find that disk SNe around lower-mass black holes (BHs) or at lower Eddington ratios are more readily detectable against the underlying AGN emission and can remain detectable over a broader range of electromagnetic bands, from the infrared to soft X-rays. However, detectability against the AGN background does not guarantee that disk SNe can be distinguished from isolated SNe with CSM interaction. We therefore further compare disk SNe with isolated SNe with and without CSM interaction and find substantial degeneracies in their macroscopic observables. Nevertheless, we identify distinctive signatures that are robust across progenitor types. The characteristic emission shifts from the EUV for \(M_{\rm BH}\lesssim10^7\,M_\odot\) toward the UV/optical for \(M_{\rm BH}=10^8\,M_\odot\), with the visibility timescale increasing from less than a day to \(\sim3\text{--}70\) days and \(T_{\rm peak}\sim3\text{--}8\) eV in the latter case. The UV/optical regime around \(10^8\,M_\odot\) BHs therefore offers particularly promising prospects for detecting disk SNe.

papers.title_en: Implementation of non-local arbitrary two-qubit controlled gates via geometric quantum computation with Rydberg anti-blockade
papers.abstract_en: In the context of Rydberg anti-blockade, this paper proposes a new scheme for a high-fidelity controlled-unitary gate based on non-adiabatic holonomic quantum computation. Under specific detuning and interaction conditions, the scheme achieves a suitable evolution path for non-adiabatic holonomic quantum computation through reverse engineering of pulse parameters. This scheme can implement arbitrary two-qubit controlled gates with favorable robustness. We also evaluate the effects of spontaneous emission and laser intensity errors on the fidelity; numerical simulations show that the geometric gate scheme still exhibits excellent performance under these errors. Furthermore, we extend the scheme to non-local gates via entanglement transfer and quantum teleportation techniques, and demonstrate its application in the mutual conversion among four-qubit entangled states (GHZ, cluster, and W states). This finding indicates the potential applicability of our scheme to complex quantum information processing tasks.

papers.title_en: Symmetry-twisted multi-entropies: Order parameters for 2D SPT phases
papers.abstract_en: Although symmetry-protected topological phases (SPTs) can be distinguished by their entanglement properties, it has been unclear how to extract this information directly from expectation values beyond the 1D case. Here, we close this gap and propose a pair of nonlocal order parameters that can detect and distinguish all bosonic SPTs in 2D protected by internal discrete, Abelian unitary symmetries. The desired topological invariants are extracted by these quantities by effectively simulating the SPT path integral on topologically non-trivial spacetime manifolds. Our order parameters are defined in terms of expectation values of partial symmetry and permutation operations acting on fixed numbers of replicas of the system in finite spatial regions. These expectation values correspond to symmetry-twisted versions of multipartite entanglement quantities known as multi-entropies. We show explicitly that our two order parameters detect symmetry-protected four-party and six-party entanglement, respectively, and we constrain possible "spurious" contributions. We analytically test our proposal in fixed-point lattice models. Our results suggest multipartite entanglement to be a defining feature of SPTs; indeed, we expect our methods to generalize to fermionic and higher-dimensional systems.

papers.title_en: Simulation of topological superconductors and their competing orders using photon-mediated interactions
papers.abstract_en: Realizing and controlling the unconventional pairing featured by topological superconductors remains a central challenge. We introduce a cavity QED quantum simulator that engineers competing chiral $p_x+ip_y$ and $d_{x^2-y^2}+id_{xy}$ orders by tailoring cavity-mediated couplings between atomic pseudospins that emulate momentum-dependent pairing channels. The desired spatially inhomogeneous cavity-mediated couplings can be engineered in a 2D optical lattice using incommensurate cavity-lattice wavelengths naturally occurring in cavity QED systems. This minimal and fully tunable platform enables controlled state preparation and continuous measurement of superconducting order parameters. To probe this competition, the platform enables selective excitation and direct time-domain detection of Bardasis-Schrieffer modes---collective excitations of the subdominant pairing channel. The same competing channel can have an even stronger impact out of equilibrium, where a sudden quench can drive its growth and abruptly reshape the dominant superconducting order, despite the stability of the dominant order in equilibrium. Together, these results establish cavity QED as a controlled setting for revealing hidden competing orders and exploring nonlinear dynamics of topological superconductivity that remain elusive in solid-state and ultracold-atom systems.

papers.title_en: Stability and dynamics of bumblebee models
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we study vector field theories with spontaneous Lorentz violation induced by a nonderivative potential $V(X)$ (with $X = B_μB^μ$), known as bumblebee models, with a Maxwell kinetic term in Minkowski spacetime. We confirm a recent result showing that a class of smooth potentials, including a purely cubic potential, leads to a Hamiltonian density that is bounded from below and assumes a global minimum for nonzero timelike expectation values of the vector field satisfying $X = b^2 > 0$, inducing spontaneous Lorentz-symmetry breaking. We show explicitly that the standard quadratic potential has a Hamiltonian that is unbounded from below and thus unstable. We analyze the Hamiltonian equations of motion for the timelike case and demonstrate that they are regular at the global minimum. Furthermore, we examine the linearized spectrum of small fluctuations around the minimum. We also study particular solutions with spherical symmetry analytically and numerically, without assuming linearization. We find that the time evolution of smooth initial configurations can develop shock-like singularities, and we explain why this behavior is expected in this model. We also identify a subset of the space of field configurations in which the field equations cease to be hyperbolic, leading to a breakdown of well-posedness of the Cauchy initial-value problem.

papers.title_en: Regge Dilaton Gravity from BF Theory
papers.abstract_en: In this work we investigate the relation between gauge and geometric descriptions of two-dimensional dilaton gravity at the level of discrete path integrals. We develop a Regge discretization of Euclidean two-dimensional dilaton gravity using homogeneously curved simplices, as well as a ribbon refined discretization of two-dimensional BF theory adapted to homogeneously curved spacetimes. For Euclidean signature and vanishing or negative cosmological constant we show how the ribbon BF discretization, through appropriate gauge fixings, leads to the Regge dilaton gravity formulation. The resulting correspondence makes explicit how a geometric Regge path integral with its associated measure emerges from its gauge theoretic formulation.

papers.title_en: Simulating cavity QED with spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensates revisited
papers.abstract_en: Simulating cavity quantum electrodynamics in synthetic platforms offers a route to studying light--matter physics without real photons. We reassess the frequently invoked analogy between harmonically trapped, spin--orbit-coupled atoms and the quantum Rabi and Dicke models, with particular emphasis on squeezing and entanglement. A single non-interacting atom realizes the quantum Rabi Hamiltonian exactly, up to elementary spin and phase-space rotations. For $N$ non-interacting atoms, however, the center-of-mass mode is only one member of a complete orthonormal set containing $N-1$ relative modes. We prove that, after all modes are included, the spin--spin terms generated by the collective mode cancel exactly against those generated by the relative modes. Equivalently, the original Hamiltonian is a sum of independent one-particle Hamiltonians and therefore cannot create interparticle entanglement from a separable state. Contact interactions invalidate this cancellation but do not remove the relative modes or turn the exact many-body Hamiltonian into a Dicke model. A one-mode Dicke description can arise only as a controlled low-energy approximation after all relevant relative excitations have been shown to be spectrally suppressed. We discuss this distinction together with experimental scales, finite temperature, and possible mode-selection strategies. We also distinguish the single-particle interference underlying density fringes from the interaction-stabilized stripe supersolid observed in many-body condensates.

papers.title_en: Testing the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the LZ event with heavy-element experiments
papers.abstract_en: We consider the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the recent 248 keV event observed by LZ and identify different experiments that could test it. Details of the underlying model and the ability of complementary experiments to test it depend significantly on the high-velocity tail of the dark matter distribution. We consider several example velocity distributions motivated by the impact of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) in order to map out the effects of this dependence. For example, we illustrate the type of high-velocity tail that would make the thermal Higgsino viable despite stringent constraints from solar neutrinos: Reducing the flux of the tail relative to simulation results improves the Higgsino fit, while extending the tail to higher velocities at fluxes below current simulation resolution evades the solar neutrino bound. This motivates more detailed simulations at higher resolution to understand the tail better. Even if xenon experiments confirm the signal event, complementary experiments are still required to test whether the underlying model is inelastic dark matter and to break degeneracies in the measurement of dark matter parameters such as mass and mass splitting. Heavy-element paleodetectors could cover most of the parameter space relevant to the LZ event. Their use of different elements could determine the dark matter mass and splitting, while their unique sensitivity to the history of the dark matter distribution could test the signal's LMC origin. Luminous detection in large neutrino detectors with heavy-element supplements could directly test the inelastic nature of the signal and measure the mass splitting, while its sensitivity to the radiative decay rate could provide strong evidence for the Higgsino interpretation.

papers.title_en: Approximate vortex lattices of atomic Fermi superfluid on a spherical surface
papers.abstract_en: While planar Fermi superfluids form Abrikosov vortex lattices under magnetic or effective gauge fields, spherical geometry forbids perfect lattices above 20 vortices. We characterize approximate vortex structures of atomic Fermi superfluids under an effective monopole field on a spherical surface as an analogue of the planar vortex-lattice problem by two constructions based on the Ginzburg-Landau theory. The first one is geometric and uses the random, geodesic-dome, and Fibonacci lattices as scaffolds to construct the order parameter from the degenerate monopole harmonics. The second one minimizes the free energy by numerically adjusting the coefficients to find the solution with the minimal Abrikosov parameter. We have verified the vortices from both constructions are zeros of the order parameter with circulating currents around the vortex cores. As the number of vortices increases, the Abrikosov parameters of both the Fibonacci-lattice and minimization solutions extrapolate to the planar value. We briefly discuss implications for ultracold atoms in thin spherical-shell geometry.

papers.title_en: A grid of fast-rotating, chemically-homogeneous, supernova and/or long-GRB progenitors
papers.abstract_en: The understanding of the mechanism(s) by which massive stars collapse and possibly explode is rapidly maturing. Uncertainties in the structure of the stellar core at the onset of collapse are often dominant in numerical simulations, and a limited number of progenitor grids are available. This is especially true for explosions where rotation and magnetic fields play a significant or primary role. We present a grid of 113 single-star models with initial masses $M_{\rm ZAMS}=30-90\,M_{\odot}$ and initial rigid rotation $ω_{\rm ZAMS}=0.5-0.99\,ω_{\rm crit}$ computed at $Z=0.001$ with the open-source stellar evolution code \textsc{MESA}. We adopt a 128-isotope nuclear reaction network capable of following the weak reactions deleptonizing the core during and after silicon core burning.
