By construction, these models experience rotationally-induced chemically-homogeneous evolution, and reach the onset of collapse ($v_{\rm infall}\lesssim -300\,\mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$) with large and structured amounts of angular momentum, possibly sufficient to form accretion disks on a proto-compact object. Therefore, these progenitor structures provide a homogeneous set of models with updated input physics and improved algorithmic accuracy to understand stellar explosions of (some types of) stripped-envelope supernovae, possibly jetted and/or broad-lined, collapsars or magnetar-powered, and/or long $γ$-ray bursts.

papers.title_en: Gram--Wishart--Stiefel formulation of the $N=2$, large--$d$ gauge theory in 1D: towards emergent Grassmannian geometry
papers.abstract_en: We develop the Gram/Wishart/Stiefel formulation of the \(N=2\), large--\(d\) planar endpoint theory of lattice BFSS/BMN matrix quantum mechanics on the lattice. The endpoint variables become rank--two Wishart eigenvalues and relative Stiefel angles, expressing the holonomy invariants \(A\), \(B\), and \(R^2=A^2+B^2\) in radial and angular Gram data. The large-\(R\) aligned contribution \(-A\) is absorbed into the Gaussian sector, producing the shifted mass \((α_Λ)_{\rm eff}=α_Λ-1/2\). The exact \(O(2)\) angular integral encodes this sector in a rank--two Bessel kernel. The pure \(-A\) theory, exactly solvable in Cartesian variables, fixes the leading Bessel/HCIZ structure: its exponential selects alignment, while its prefactor removes the spurious doubled Wishart entropy. We then apply this structure to the transverse \(B\)-type expansion and its non-polynomial toy completion. Finite polynomial truncations lead to an apparent large--\(d\) perturbativity bound incompatible with the continuum limit, but this bound is shown to be an artifact of truncation. After summing the local transverse completion and balancing the compensating \(+A\) term, the Wishart saddle is recovered with the physical shifted mass. The resulting continuum behavior reproduces the universal \(-2d\) contribution of the \(D_Λ\)-channel, while the genuinely anisotropic \(β_Λ\)-channel lies outside the scope of a pure transverse \(B\)-type description. Finally, we outline the emergent Grassmannian geometry encoded by the two endpoint planes. Their relative angular fluctuations form a \(2(d-2)\)-dimensional sector, whose entropy interpretation is developed in the sequel. For \(d\ge4\), the two planes generically span a relational four-dimensional subspace of \(\mathbb R^d\).

papers.title_en: monoprop: Scaling Pauli and Majorana propagation via Anticommutation Indices
papers.abstract_en: We introduce monoprop, an open-source, massively parallel operator-propagation framework for fermion and qubit bases. For $N$ qubits or modes, existing codes represent each of the $K$ tracked operator terms (Pauli strings or products of Majorana operators) as a $2N$-bit string, testing each for anticommutation with the gate at $O(KN)$ cost per gate. Here, we introduce the anticommutation index which rapidly looks up the terms anticommuting with a gate. A local gate changes only the terms that touch its sites, and when terms are truncated to act on few sites, only a fraction $\sim1/N$ touch any given qubit or mode, and we use this to prove the time per gate scales as $O(K/N)$. This counterintuitive result tells us that for a fixed number of terms, increasing the number of sites can make things faster. We demonstrate this numerically, and show monoprop scales almost ideally to 8192 cores, tracking $9.5\times10^{10}$ terms. Beyond propagation, we present memory-efficient surrogate graphs, which record one propagation and replay it at new angles, for fast energy re-estimation and parameter gradients, and an efficient method for finding energy-minimising gates and optimal angles for simulating adaptive quantum-chemistry circuits.

papers.title_en: Entropic force in matrix
papers.abstract_en: We consider the entropic force in matrix theory. We find the gravity in bulk can be emergent from the entropic force.

papers.title_en: Quantum-Corrected and Hairy Black Holes via Analogue Gravity
papers.abstract_en: This thesis maps two exotic black-hole geometries onto the transonic flow of a de Laval nozzle and reads their perturbative response in aerodynamic variables. The first is the hairy black hole of gravitational decoupling, constrained by the dominant energy condition and by the existence of a horizon. The second is the Calmet-Kuipers metric, short-ranged and governed by the single Wilson coefficient of the dimension-six operator that the two-loop Goroff-Sagnotti divergence identifies. Perturbations of spin 0, 1/2, 1 and 2 reduce to a Schrödinger-type wave equation, whose spectrum the Mashhoon method returns as a whole overtone tower in closed form, every frequency damped. The two corrections are distinguished by which channel responds and by how strongly all of them do, the quantum coupling moving the quality factor by up to 37% in the scalar and Dirac channels and by about 10% in the other two, while the hair acts on every channel alike. Identifying the two tortoise coordinates turns the equality of the potentials into a Sturm-Liouville problem, so that the prescribed barrier fixes the wall profile and with it the flow variables and the thrust coefficient. The hair is felt across the whole divergent section, whereas the quantum correction registers only near the throat and grows as the inverse fourth power of the mass, which confines it to primordial black holes. The analogy is kinematical, so the duct reproduces the scattering of perturbations off these geometries without reproducing the field equations behind them.

papers.title_en: The Kick Velocities of Neutron Stars in Binary Systems
papers.abstract_en: Neutron stars (NSs) receive natal kicks on their formation in supernovae (SNe). We consider constraints placed on the natal kick magnitudes by NSs in different classes of binary systems. We compare observed systems to predictions from the COMPAS rapid population synthesis code, where we apply kick models with varied natal kick prescriptions. Specifically, we compare binary orbits (i.e., periods and eccentricities) and systemic kick estimates of (1) Gaia observations of NS-harboring binaries (Gaia NSs), (2) NS low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs), (3) NS-white dwarf binaries (NSWDs), (4) NS high-mass X-ray binaries (HMXBs) and in particular Be X-ray binaries (BeXBs), and (5) double NSs (DNSs). In this comparison, we find that we can reproduce most of the observed properties of the Gaia NSs, LMXBs, and NSWDs with natal kicks calibrated to the velocities of young isolated pulsars, although we need a small amount of "rocket" kicks to explain the Gaia NS eccentricities. The HMXBs and DNSs, in contrast, show evidence of significantly reduced NS natal kicks. In particular, we find that an apparent correlation between eccentricity and systemic kick for DNSs can be explained by Blaauw kicks, if the natal kicks are $\lesssim 10$ km s$^{-1}$. Although our model does not align well with low-metallicity Gaia NSs, high-eccentricity BeXBs, and DNS mass estimates, we provide alternative hypothetical explanations for these systems. We conclude that a model in which NSs that are formed in binaries with high-mass companions receive significantly reduced natal kicks can provide a relatively consistent explanation for the observed NSs in binary systems.

papers.title_en: Disentangling geometry & growth in cosmic neutrino mass constraints: a more physical split and diagnostic
papers.abstract_en: Recent cosmological data hint at a neutrino mass sum below the minimum value allowed by the neutrino mass oscillation experiments, with a preference for the opposite of massive neutrinos ("negative" neutrino masses). Since massive neutrinos impact the expansion history of the Universe, which in turn modifies the growth of structure, we ask whether such a preference originates from the observed geometry or structure growth, and whether the two agree. In this paper, we introduce a more physical split of $\sum m_ν$ into parameters $\sum m_ν^{geo}$ and $\sum m_ν^{growth}$ based on their physical effects, with extension to negative values. We split the expansion rate at the Boltzmann-code level: $\sum m_ν^{geo}$ sets $H(z)$ for distance computation, and $\sum m_ν^{growth}$ sets $H(z)$ for perturbation evolution. Combining Planck primary CMB, Planck+ACT+SPT CMB lensing and DESI BAO data, we find similar sensitivity and "negative" preference from geometry and growth with $\sum m_ν^{geo} = -0.07\pm0.10$ eV (68% C.L.) and $\sum m_ν^{growth} = -0.13^{+0.10}_{-0.12}$ eV (68% C.L.). The difference of the two is a null test of the $Λ$CDM model, passed by current data at $0.4σ$ level. Forecasts on Advanced SO CMB and DESI DR3 BAO show that $0.058$ eV would be rejected at $3.0σ$ from the geometry channel alone, if the negative mean of $\sum m_ν^{geo} = -0.07$ eV persists. The two channels can also provide a powerful new diagnostic between possible origins of the neutrino mass tension. With future CMB and BAO data, our Fisher forecasts show that an incorrect dark energy model displaces $\sum m_ν^{geo}$ from $0.058$ eV by $3.1$-$4.2σ$ and $\sum m_ν^{growth}$ by $1.1$-$1.3σ$, while an underestimated reionization optical depth reverses the pattern, $2.7$-$3.6σ$ in $\sum m_ν^{growth}$ against at most $0.23σ$ in $\sum m_ν^{geo}$. (Abridged)

papers.title_en: A model for the image structure and spectral energy distribution of relativistic jets
papers.abstract_en: Upcoming advances in high-frequency VLBI promise to enable spatially resolved studies of astrophysical jets across an increasingly large source population. We present here a Python implementation of the semi-analytic model from Tsunetoe et al. (2025) for self-consistently interpreting the spatial and spectral structure of the synchrotron emission from such jets. The model is based on an axisymmetric force-free jet solution supplemented with a prescription for nonthermal electron heating, synchrotron cooling, pitch-angle anisotropy in the electron distribution, and radiative transfer along straight rays. We use this model to explore how the predicted spectral energy distribution depends on the model parameters, identifying approximately self-similar scalings with black hole mass, accretion rate, and electron heating efficiency. We also compare the model predictions against observations of M87 and Sgr A*. For M87, a single fiducial parameter set qualitatively reproduces VLBI images across multiple frequencies and matches the observed longitudinal intensity profile, while also yielding a broadband SED that is quantitatively consistent with the observed radio through X-ray measurements. For Sgr A*, a fit to the quiescent-state SED demonstrates that emission from a collimated jet with comparable nonthermal heating efficiency to M87's is quantitatively consistent with the observed radio through X-ray measurements, predicting a compact jet whose radio size decreases inversely with frequency, consistent with VLBI constraints.

papers.title_en: JWST reveals a highly ionized nebula powered by an ultraluminous X-ray source with a massive black hole in the metal-poor galaxy Holmberg II
papers.abstract_en: Recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations have revealed fine-structure lines of ions with ionization potentials ${\gtrsim}50$\,eV, such as [Ne\,{\sc v}] and [O\,{\sc iv}], in nebular spectra of some low-metallicity galaxies, raising questions about the nature of the ionizing sources. Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) have been considered as potential contributors, but direct evidence linking individual ULXs to highly ionized nebulae is limited. Here we present JWST IFU spectroscopy of the nebula surrounding the template ULX Ho\,II\,X--1 in the low-metallicity galaxy Holmberg\,II, already known to emit He\,{\sc ii}\,$\lambda4686$ and [O\,{\sc iv}]\,25.89\,$μ$m lines. We resolve the infrared nebula on spatial scales of ${\sim}15-25$\,pc and report the first detections of [Ne\,{\sc v}] and [Ne\,{\sc vi}] in this source. We find anisotropic ionizing conditions: emission from the highest-ionization species arises from compact regions offset from the ULX toward the previously detected radio knots, whereas lower-ionization species trace the wider nebula. The preferential alignment of the highest-ionization emission with the radio axis suggests anisotropic escape of the ionizing continuum and a physical connection with jet-ejection activity. Spectral lines across the nebula are narrow and consistent with the instrumental resolution, indicating kinematically quiescent gas and disfavoring shocks as the dominant ionization mechanism. Together, these results provide direct evidence linking an individual ULX to a highly ionized nebula in a low-metallicity galaxy. These JWST observations of Ho~II~X--1 show that an accreting black hole in a low-metallicity galaxy is responsible for the extreme ionization of the surrounding nebula on ${\sim}100$\,pc scales.

papers.title_en: Bulk-dissociated topological bands without spin-orbit coupling in hetero-dimensional superconducting metamaterials
papers.abstract_en: Topological superconductors (TSCs) in superconducting hybrid heterostructures, which integrate superconducting and non-superconducting materials, have been intensely investigated with the hope of discovering exotic non-Abelian anyons for fault-tolerant quantum computing. In this effort, a challenge for hybrid superconducting systems is controlling hybridization, which is often a balance between enhancing the superconducting proximity effect at the cost of suppressing desirable electronic properties such as strong spin-orbit interactions. Hence, discovering hybrid superconducting systems with topological properties controlled and enhanced by material geometry design without spin-orbit interactions would be intriguing to explore. In this work, we theoretically study a square superconducting network decorated with spin-polarized magnetic adatoms. We find that localized Yu-Shiba-Rusinov bound states at magnetic adatom sites collectively form a weak topological superconducting phase despite the absence of spin-orbit interactions. We then demonstrate that by tuning the Fermi energy of the network, the system can transition from a weak TSC phase to a bulk-dissociated TSC phase where the edge state bands separate from the bulk, giving rise to unexpected features such as nodal lines and co-existing bulk-dissociated edge and corner modes. Moreover, our findings highlight how hetero-dimensional superconducting metamaterials can serve as a useful template for controlling the coupling and dissociation between electronic degrees of freedom of different dimensionalities.

papers.title_en: Local supersymmetry implies momentum map/Gauntlett-Pakis equations and vanishing generalized Komar forms
papers.abstract_en: The first-order differential equations satisfied by Killing spinor bilinears (momentum map equations or Gauntlett--Pakis equations, Killing vector equations and the vanishing of the generalized Komar charge of the supersymmetric Killing vector) can be derived directly from the action of the local supersymmetry algebra on bosonic fields. We show how this comes about in several examples of increasing complexity, one of which is 11-dimensional supergravity.

papers.title_en: Self Calibrated Galaxy Groups from the DESI DR1 Bright Galaxy Survey
papers.abstract_en: We present a galaxy group catalog built from Data Release 1 of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Bright Galaxy Survey, using the Self Calibrated Group Finder. The algorithm uses clustering data from the observed sample to calibrate the Group Finder's free parameters, rather than simulations. The catalog contains 2,229,741 galaxies from ~$2680$ deg$^2$ of sky with 3-pass coverage and $r$-band fluxes $\lt 19.5$. The catalog classifies all galaxies in the flux-limited sample as centrals or satellites and estimates host dark matter halo masses. We show the satellite fraction $f_{\rm sat}$, luminosity halo mass relation, stellar halo mass relation and halo occupation distributions (HODs) from the catalog. We find these non-parametric HODs can be fit by standard HOD models, with satellite power-law index $α$ values around 0.75 for star-forming galaxies and around 1.1 for quiescent objects. In agreement with recent results, we find that the quenched fraction of central galaxies depends mostly on halo mass and is nearly independent of central galaxy stellar mass for galaxies more massive than $10^{10.3}$ $M_\odot h^{-1}$ and halos more massive than $10^{12.2}$ $M_\odot h^{-1}$. In an appendix, we introduce a new Hybrid Nearest Neighbor (HNN) technique to mitigate systematics from fiber incompleteness. HNN uses photometric redshifts and multiple on-sky neighbors to assign redshifts to unobserved targets. Calibrated on DESI Survey Validation 3 data, our technique yields correct redshifts $\sim 50\%$ of the time and produces unbiased halo occupation statistics.

papers.title_en: Equality of the Jellium and the Uniform Electron Gas Energies
papers.abstract_en: Jellium, a system of electrons in a uniform neutralizing background, and the uniform electron gas (UEG), a system of electrons with constant density and no background, are two standard models of the electron gas. We prove that the ground-state energy per unit volume of Jellium, as defined by Lieb and Narnhofer, coincides with the UEG energy defined by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer, i.e. \[ e^\hbar_{\rm Jel}(ρ_0)=e^\hbar_{\rm UEG}(ρ_0). \] This equality was previously established in the classical case by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer and independently by Cotar and Petrache.

papers.title_en: Jittering jets in stripped-envelope core-collapse supernovae
papers.abstract_en: We compare the expected explosion time of core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) in the jittering jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) to that in the neutrino-driven (the delayed neutrino) mechanism, and conclude that for most, but not all, stellar models, even when the neutrino-driven mechanism might have led to an explosion, the JJEM starts to operate before the neutrino mechanism fully revives the stalled shock. To achieve this goal, we conduct comprehensive one-dimensional stellar evolution simulations using the code \textsc{mesa} to determine the expected explosion time according to the JJEM, which corresponds to the time when the inner convective layer of the core is accreted onto the newly born neutron star (NS). We present results for many hydrogen-rich, hydrogen-stripped, and helium+hydrogen-stripped envelope CCSN progenitor models. We find that most, but not all, of our models in the initial mass range of $M_{\rm ZAMS}=12M_\odot$ to $M_{\rm ZAMS}=40M_\odot$, have at least one strong convective zone inside the mass coordinate that is the maximum baryonic mass of an NS, $m \simeq 2.65\ M_\odot$, which can facilitate the JJEM. This study contributes to establishing the JJEM as a viable explosion mechanism of CCSNe.

papers.title_en: Casimir Sign Reversal from Finite-Range Bogoliubov Fluctuations
papers.abstract_en: We study the zero-temperature Casimir effect of a three-dimensional Bose fluid with finite-range corrections to its Bogoliubov spectrum. Beyond the universal acoustic contribution scaling as $L^{-3}$, the long-distance expansion contains a nonuniversal $L^{-5}$ correction that can compete with the phononic term. We derive this crossover analytically within a minimal isotropic finite-range model and test the asymptotic result against the full dispersion. A regulator-independent Poisson-resummed calculation confirms that sign reversals of the Casimir energy are possible, while showing that the apparent low-coupling zero inferred by balancing only the $L^{-3}$ and $L^{-5}$ terms is not quantitatively controlled. Robust sign changes instead occur in the stable regime close to roton softening, where the Casimir energy acquires an oscillatory finite-momentum contribution. Strongly dipolar atomic gases provide a natural motivation for microscopic interaction lengths in the nanometric regime. We further discuss how the resulting nonlinear force law could be probed through the frequency response of a driven nanomechanical resonator.

papers.title_en: FUGUE: A New GPU-accelerated General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics Code with Weak-Field Multipole Self-Gravity and Quasi-Stationary Kerr Black Hole Evolution
papers.abstract_en: We present FUGUE, a new GPU-accelerated code for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD). The code supports an optional quasi-stationary update of the Kerr black hole mass and spin, as well as weak-field multipole self-gravity computed with a spherical harmonic Poisson solver. The calculations using high-order multipoles in the Poisson solver are expensive, so the self-gravity solver is well suited for GPU acceleration. The code uses shock-capturing methods and a second-order Runge--Kutta (RK2) scheme for time integration. We validate the code with hydrodynamic, magnetohydrodynamic, general relativistic, and convergence tests for the self-gravity module. We present an application of the code to a simulation of a self-gravitating, Toomre-unstable, magnetized accretion disk with a mass of 1,M-Sun around a Kerr black hole. In our demonstration model, gravitational instabilities are associated with changes in the mass accretion rate and the Blandford--Znajek luminosity, and may contribute to gamma-ray burst variability.The performance of the code is equivalent to or exceeds that of the current state-of-the-art GRMHD codes, achieving more than 470 million zone-cycles per second on a single NVIDIA GH200 GPU with linear reconstruction.

papers.title_en: Co-design of ground-based gravitational wave detector networks
papers.abstract_en: Discussions around the design philosophy and location of the next generation of ground-based gravitational wave detectors are still underway. In this context, we propose IfoScout, an innovative methodology for detector co-design based on state-of-the-art machine-learning (ML) techniques. As a simple demonstration, we present a two-stage simulation of a network of fictional L-shaped interferometers whose sensitivity is optimized within physical and geographical constraints, indirectly resulting in reducing the costs. To achieve this, we gather publicly available data for two token locations and establish the length and orientation with reinforcement learning (RL). Next, we optimize the internal detector parameters related to cavity stability to achieve the best possible sensitivity by means of differential programming (DP). We make the case that pipelines such as IfoScout could have a positive impact on the final design of new generation detectors (e.g. the Einstein Telescope, the Cosmic Explorer, etc.), given precise data and detailed, realistic simulations of the interferometers.

papers.title_en: Radio Continuum Study of One of the Brightest Large Magellanic Cloud Supernova Remnants N 132D
papers.abstract_en: We present a new radio continuum study of the Large Magellanic Cloud supernova remnant N 132D using observations from the Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA) and MeerKAT. The radio morphology shows a clear spatial correlation with the X-ray emission in the central and left regions of the remnant, as well as in the right portion of the shell, indicating a close connection between the thermal and non-thermal plasma components. Polarisation measurements reveal predominantly radial magnetic fields, with mean fractional polarisations of 1.2 per cent, 3.0 per cent, and 4.0 per cent at 2100, 5500, and 9000 MHz, respectively. There is also a complex structure in the Faraday Depth spectrum, showing a double-peaked profile that indicates regions with differing magnetisation properties or varying magnetic field geometry. The rotation measure derived from ATCA data has an average value of ~2 rad m^-2, with a maximum of ~338 rad m^-2. We estimate a constant partition magnetic field of ~90 microG and a minimum energy of 3 x 10^50 erg, which is in a constant partition between the energy density of electrons and the energy density of the magnetic field. The integrated radio spectrum follows a power law with a spectral index of -0.74 +- 0.01. These results provide new constraints on the magnetic field structure and energetic properties of N 132D and offer insight into particle acceleration and shock evolution in young supernova remnants.

papers.title_en: Beyond the polynomial ansatz: regular $AdS_3\times M_8$ solutions of M-theory
papers.abstract_en: We study regular compact solutions of the cohomogeneity-one $AdS_3\times M_8$ system of Gauntlett, Mac Conamhna, Mateos and Waldram, where $M_8$ is an $S^2$ bundle over three constant-curvature Riemann surfaces. We find that an endpoint argument rules out every non-flat curvature-sign sector without a positive-curvature factor, while an analytic deformation gives regular families with four radial shape parameters in all remaining sectors, with the base geometry held fixed. The known polynomial solutions form a proper analytic locus in these families. Non-polynomiality is therefore generic in parameter space, although the deviation from an endpoint-matching polynomial can be very small. Apart from the completely flat exception, the curvature-sign criterion is necessary and sufficient within this ansatz. Four magnetic flux ratios give local coordinates near the reference solution and its small-curvature deformations, and a rational inverse reconstructs candidate endpoint data directly from finite flux ratios. In the fully positive sector we prove that one explicit four-dimensional finite-ratio neighbourhood lies inside the physical flux image. The magnetic periods and leading holographic central charge reduce to endpoint data, and, once the common Brown--Henneaux normalization is fixed, the nontrivial flux dependence of the equivariant localization formula agrees with the endpoint result as an exact algebraic identity. We also quantify the non-polynomial corrections and analyse finite degenerations under explicit convergence hypotheses.

papers.title_en: Study of pulse jitter characteristics of PSR J1744-1134: Towards high precision pulsar timing with InPTA
papers.abstract_en: Variations in the shapes of individual pulses introduce a broadband noise component in pulsar times of arrival beyond what is expected from radiometer noise, referred to as the jitter noise. This noise limits the timing accuracy and, consequently, the sensitivity required for the detection of nanohertz gravitational waves using pulsar timing arrays. Accurate characterization of jitter noise, including its amplitude and frequency dependence, is therefore essential for each pulsar. In this work, we present the first detailed study of jitter noise in PSR J1744-1134 over the frequency range 300-500 MHz, using observations from the Indian Pulsar Timing Array experiment conducted with the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope. We detect clear signatures of jitter in this pulsar through pulse-level analysis and Bayesian inference. Furthermore, we investigated the frequency dependence of the jitter noise and compared our results with earlier measurements at higher frequencies. The observed differences in jitter amplitude suggest a possible frequency evolution, highlighting the importance of low-frequency studies for improving pulsar timing precision and accuracy. We also investigated the effect of jitter on the high precision dispersion measure derived from our observations and found that jitter is not the limiting factor for DM precision achieved for this pulsar in the given observation timescale.

papers.title_en: Exact AdS and pp-waves in multi-gravity beyond pairwise interactions
papers.abstract_en: We construct exact anti-de Sitter (AdS) waves and pp-waves in ghost-free multi-gravity beyond pairwise interactions for an arbitrary number $\mathcal{N}$ of vielbeins, in any spacetime dimension $D\geq3$. Deforming proportional AdS and Minkowski solutions along a common null direction reduces the full nonlinear field equations to coupled linear differential equations for the wave profiles, without restricting their amplitudes. The system is diagonalised in the same eigenbasis as the perturbative Fierz-Pauli mass matrix, separating the solutions into one massless and $\mathcal{N}-1$ massive eigenprofiles. We obtain explicit radial and transverse solutions and impose an AdS boundary falloff. This falloff admits the appropriate radial branch of every mode with non-negative squared mass and excludes profiles with negative squared masses, including logarithmic solutions at the Breitenlohner-Freedman threshold. We also relate the AdS waves to pp-waves through a local flat limit. Explicit examples exhibit wave configurations that cannot be reproduced by ghost-free pairwise theories, demonstrating that genuine multi-field interactions support new exact gravitational-wave solutions.

papers.title_en: Fermi Acceleration Mechanisms Beyond Lorentz Symmetry
papers.abstract_en: We construct models for first- and second-order Fermi acceleration of particles, incorporating generic frame transformations, dispersion relations, and conservation laws. Within this framework, we study deformations of Lorentz symmetry via the $κ$-Poincaré algebra in the bicrossproduct and classical bases, which respectively deform and preserve the relativistic dispersion relation. We also examine explicit Lorentz symmetry violation and compare the results with deformed relativity and special relativity. The energy spectra present different shapes when one considers deformation or violation of Lorentz symmetry in superluminal or subluminal scenarios. One of the possible outcomes is an intense decay of the spectrum for higher energies. We also gather the predictions of all the scenarios considered, comparing the spectra produced at the source in the energy domain, which is the variable in which cosmic ray observatories report their measurements.

papers.title_en: The three- and four-loop equal-mass sunset integrals and local Calabi--Yau fourfolds and fivefolds
papers.abstract_en: We determine the equal-mass two-dimensional three- and four-loop sunset Feynman integrals $I^{(3)}_\circleddash$ and $I^{(4)}_\circleddash$ at large Euclidean momentum in terms of the genus-zero Gromov--Witten theory of the local Calabi--Yau fourfold and fivefold $X_L=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_L})$, where $F_L\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{L+1}$, $L=3,4$, is a smooth hypersurface of multidegree $(1,\ldots,1)$. At two loops the sunset integral is governed by the prepotential of a local Calabi--Yau threefold. For $L\geq3$ the moduli spaces of unmarked stable maps have positive virtual dimension and there is no prepotential, therefore the Feynman integral is governed instead by the one-point potential $\mathcal F_{γ_L}$ with insertion $γ_L=H^{L-1}/(L-1)!$, by its gravitational descendants, and by $ζ(3)$ boundary terms coming from the Gamma class. At both loop orders the coefficient of $R^{L-1}$ in the Frobenius expansion in the mirror coordinate $R$ is $-θ_Q\mathcal F_{γ_L}$ with the Novikov variable $Q=\exp(R)$. At three loops the whole Feynman integral is an explicit expression in $\mathcal F_{γ_3}$ alone, because genus-zero recursion determines all descendant series from it; at four loops two diagonal series suffice, and the $ζ(3)$ term is itself corrected by $θ_Q\mathcal F_{γ_4}$. At three loops we also derive the analytic normalization independently, from the Picard--Fuchs equation and the polar part of a Mellin transform, prove integrality of the multiple-cover transforms for arbitrary integral insertions together with an explicit quantum-$K$ formula, and compute the exact period connection polynomials. Finally we give endpoint values along the Euclidean axis, bounds on the Taylor radii in the Novikov variable $Q$, a computer-assisted proof of the four-loop endpoint nonanalyticity, and a comparison of the normalizations at two, three and four loops.

papers.title_en: All three-loop four-point massless integrals with one off-shell leg
papers.abstract_en: We present the complete set of massless three-loop four-point master integrals with one off-shell external leg. These are essential building blocks for the three-loop virtual corrections to Higgs-boson or vector-boson production in association with a jet at the Large Hadron Collider, required for next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD predictions. We construct a complete basis of canonical integrals by identifying integrands with simple poles and unit leading singularities, solely by integrand analysis. This includes an integral family with 371 master integrals and a 19-dimensional top sector. The solutions for all relevant integrals are provided as a map to a minimal set of iterated integrals graded according to their analytic properties, together with high-precision series expansions.

papers.title_en: Equal-mass sunset integrals and genus-zero local Gromov--Witten theory of Calabi--Yau $n$-folds
papers.abstract_en: We prove an exact identity, as convergent logarithmic germs at large Euclidean momentum, between the equal-mass two-dimensional $(n-1)$-loop sunset Feynman integral, with $n\geq4$, and the genus-zero one-point descendant invariants of the local Calabi--Yau $n$-fold $X_n=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_n})$, where $F_n\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{n}$ is a smooth $(1,\ldots,1)$ hypersurface. Writing $s$ for the momentum variable and $y=-1/s$, the identity reads \[ I^{(n-1)}_{\circleddash}(s)=(-1)^{n-1}yA\,\Bigl[nR^{n-1}-θ_Q{\mathcal D}_0^Δ\,R^{n-2} +\sum_{j=0}^{n-3}c_jR^j\Bigr], \] where $R=\log y+O(y)$ is the local mirror coordinate, $A=θ_yR$, $Q=e^R$, ${\mathcal D}_0^Δ(Q)$ is the primary one-point potential, and each $c_j$ has the form \[ c_j=c_j^{(0)}+\sum_{a=0}^{n-2}\bigl(c_{j,a}\,{\mathcal D}_a^Δ(Q) +c'_{j,a}\,θ_Q{\mathcal D}_a^Δ(Q)\bigr) \] with the coefficients in $\mathbb Q[ζ(3),ζ(5),\ldots]$ the odd zeta values coming from the Gamma class. The descendant series ${\mathcal D}_a^Δ(Q)$ are given explicitly by the ambient hypergeometric series and the inverse mirror map. We also prove global univalence of the principal mirror map, with explicit upper and lower bounds on the $Q$-Taylor radii, extract the full primary evaluation divisor and its integral cover transform, and reduce the ambient endpoint constants to a finite universal Gamma-class part and $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ real parameters.

papers.title_en: Quantum Superposition Principle and Geometry
papers.abstract_en: If one takes seriously the postulate of quantum mechanics in which physical states are rays in the standard Hilbert space of the theory, one is naturally lead to a geometric formulation of the theory. Within this formulation of quantum mechanics, the resulting description is very elegant from the geometrical viewpoint, since it allows to cast the main postulates of the theory in terms of two geometric structures, namely a symplectic structure and a Riemannian metric. However, the usual superposition principle of quantum mechanics is not naturally incorporated, since the quantum state space is non-linear. In this note we offer some steps to incorporate the superposition principle within the geometric description. In this respect, we argue that it is necessary to make the distinction between a 'projective superposition principle' and a 'decomposition principle' that extend the standard superposition principle. We illustrate our proposal with two very well known examples, namely the spin 1/2 system and the two slit experiment, where the distinction is clear from the physical perspective. We show that the two principles have also a different mathematical origin within the geometrical formulation of the theory.

papers.title_en: Generalised entanglement wedges in three dimensions
papers.abstract_en: Generalized entanglement wedges (GWs), proposed by Bousso and Penington for gravitating regions in general spacetimes, share many properties of ordinary entanglement wedges, including nesting, monotonicity and strong subadditivity of their generalized entropies. In AdS/CFT, the corresponding properties of entanglement wedges are consequences of the structure of the dual CFT. In this paper we ask whether the properties of GWs have a similar origin. We explore this question in vacuum AdS$_3$ at leading order in $G$. We first show that every GW on a static slice is a union of geodesically convex regions. Each such region is an intersection of ordinary entanglement wedges, so every GW is built from unions and intersections of entanglement wedges. We then use the Crofton formula of integral geometry to write the perimeter of a convex region as the measure of the set of geodesics that intersect it. In AdS$_3$ every geodesic is the Ryu--Takayanagi surface of a boundary interval, so this measure can be written in terms of the von Neumann entropies of CFT intervals. Strong subadditivity of the CFT entropy guarantees that the measure is positive. Monotonicity and strong subadditivity of GWs then follow from simple inequalities between sets of geodesics. The strong subadditivity of GWs is therefore a direct consequence of strong subadditivity on the boundary. Our results further suggest that GWs correspond to subsystems of the CFT that are more general than boundary subregions.

papers.title_en: Collective Organization of String Fragmentation
papers.abstract_en: How coherent confining strings reorganize into hadronic matter is a central open problem in nonequilibrium gauge dynamics. Using real-time tensor-network simulations of the massive Schwinger model, we identify a collective organization underlying string fragmentation. For intermediate masses, the dynamics simplifies and more than $99\%$ of the temporal evolution of the electric-field probability distribution is governed by a single collective mode whose decay tracks the survival probability of the parent string. The extracted survival law exhibits the same Gaussian dependence implied by the Lund world-sheet area law, providing microscopic support for its characteristic area law dependence without assuming the Lund fragmentation mechanism. The same mode controls the transition from the coherent string to the produced mesons, explains the universal non-thermal effective fluid equation of state, and essentially controls the growth of bipartite entanglement through the causal propagation of massive pairs. These results identify collective fragmentation as an organizing principle of coherent string breaking and provide a microscopic perspective on the dynamical origin of a central ingredient of Lund hadronization.

papers.title_en: ACT stands for Awkward Cosmology Theories
papers.abstract_en: Recent Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) observations, combined with Planck, favor a scalar spectral index in tension with Starobinsky inflation. Two main strategies have been proposed to reconcile Starobinsky inflation with these data: (i) including higher-curvature operators in the gravitational action, and (ii) modifying the post-inflationary reheating dynamics. We critically re-examine both approaches. When higher-curvature corrections are included, dimensional-analysis arguments allow introducing a second mass scale suppressing higher-dimensional operators, resulting in a one-coupling, two-scale effective theory. We show that fitting the ACT data drives this class of effective theories toward a regime of stronger sensitivity to UV physics, potentially implying fine-tuning of the inflationary observables. We illustrate our general point with two concrete models, namely no-scale supergravity and metric-affine gravity, showing that they provide different realizations of the same underlying $f(R)$ theory. On the reheating side, requiring the CMB modes to re-enter the horizon before recombination leads to stringent constraints on the reheating equation of state, and fitting the ACT data favors an exotic reheating phase with $ω_{\rm reh} > 1/3$, incompatible with inflaton oscillations about the minimum of the standard Starobinsky potential. Finally, we explore the possibility that a phase of cosmological stasis, driven by a tower of decaying massive states, could play the role of the post-inflationary epoch. We find that accommodating ACT-preferred $n_s$ in this setup requires a tower of states with negative energy density. Taken together, our results suggest that reconciling Starobinsky inflation with the ACT data demands ingredients that are challenging to motivate from the perspective of UV-complete theories, undermining the minimality of the original Starobinsky model.

papers.title_en: Infinite magic and the emergence of the continuum
papers.abstract_en: Which features of a quantum state are needed for a relativistic quantum field theory to emerge from a lattice system? We address this question by establishing a quantitative relationship between the type classification of hyperfinite von Neumann algebras and the quantum-information-theoretic resource of nonstabilizerness, also called magic. Our results establish two complementary parts of this relationship. First, we prove that any stabilizer system on a lattice defines a canonical GNS Hilbert space in which local von Neumann algebras do not contain type III factors in their central decomposition. As an explicit example, we prove that for stabilizer systems with short-range order, the local algebras are isomorphic to tensor products of hyperfinite factors of type I or type II. This demonstrates that the absence of magic is accompanied by the absence of type III factors in the local algebras, therefore prohibiting the appearance of a quantum field theory. Second, for the hyperfinite factors of Araki, Woods and Powers, we prove a quantitative equivalence: The limiting factor is of type III if and only if the locally optimized min-relative entropy of magic diverges. This divergence is necessary to generate the continuous spectrum associated to a type III factor. Thus, in this setting, the emergence of a type III factor requires not merely the presence of magic, but an infinite amount of it. These results provide a rigorous setting supporting the proposal that infinite magic is a necessary structural ingredient for the emergence of a relativistic continuum from lattice systems.

papers.title_en: Optimal Strategies for Gravitational-Wave Memory Detection with Noise Marginalization in Pulsar Timing Arrays
papers.abstract_en: Current pulsar timing arrays could detect gravitational wave memory, which would provide a unique test of general relativity. In order to optimize our searches for gravitational wave memory in pulsar timing arrays, we integrate the optimal frequentist statistics for GW memory into the \texttt{enterprise} code suite. We additionally test a noise marginalized version of this statistic, and compare it's effectiveness to the simpler maximum posterior method. We perform these tests on simulated pulsar timing array with red and white noise content, as well as the NANOGrav $15$-year data set. We find no significant variations in our detection statistics between the noise-marginalized and the maximum-posterior methods for the simulated datasets, and only small variations in the NANOGrav $15$-year comparisons. We conclude that for realistic PTAs the noise-marginalization method could be useful for assigning a false alarm probability to Bayesian results, though the maximum posterior method is sufficient for identifying potentially detectable signals.

papers.title_en: All Order Gravitational Wave Tails for Subleading Post-Newtonian Expansion
papers.abstract_en: The low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. In the Newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. At the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in Newton's constant $G$. We extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-Newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. We consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. The correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic Newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. Its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. For $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. Our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier work arXiv:2610.07134.

papers.title_en: The Magic Barrier: A Universal Feature of Quantum Thermalization
papers.abstract_en: We show that the emergence of a ``magic barrier'', characterized by a transient maximum of nonstabilizerness during rapid entanglement growth, is a universal feature of thermalization within quantum ergodic theories, which is intimately connected to random matrix spectral properties. Starting from a pure product state, we analytically determine the time evolution of entanglement entropy, antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal trace distance magic under unitary dynamics generated by random matrix Hamiltonians drawn from all three Gaussian ensembles. We find that the transient maxima of antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal magic occur on the same characteristic timescale as the maximum rate of entanglement growth. These results establish that the magic barrier is a universal feature of RMT thermalization, suggesting universality across quantum chaotic systems. We conclude that quantitative simulations of thermalization in ergodic quantum theories inherently require quantum computation.

papers.title_en: JWST lensed quasar dark matter survey V: Hints of self-interacting dark matter from 29 quadruply imaged quasars
papers.abstract_en: Theories of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) predict the eventual core collapse of dark matter halos, a process that transforms these structures into extremely efficient gravitational lenses. We present a population-level inference on the abundance of core collapsed halos and subhalos in the mass range $10^6 - 10^{10.7} M_{\odot}$ using 29 quadruply imaged quasars, drawing on the collective lensing signal of many low-mass perturbers. Our structure formation model predicts the abundance of collapsed (sub)halos as a function of halo mass and redshift. We quantify how our results are affected by systematic uncertainties, including the abundance of globular clusters (GCs) and subhalos, and the internal structure of deeply collapsed halos. Our data exhibits a strong preference for core collapsed halos in the lens model, with Bayes factors disfavoring CDM relative to SIDM ranging from 8:1 to 24:1, depending on the assumed SIDM subhalo abundance and the internal structure of collapsed halos. Explaining our data without core collapse requires both a GC abundance well above expectations and more subhalos than predicted by $N$-body simulations. These results pose a challenge to the CDM paradigm. We present a particle physics interpretation of these results in a companion paper.

papers.title_en: Spread Complexity for Local Operator Quenches with Conserved Momentum
papers.abstract_en: We study a family of locally excited states in two-dimensional conformal field theories in different setups, defined on the plane, on the cylinder, or at finite temperature. These states are constructed by assigning independent chiral and anti-chiral regulators to a local primary operator, leading to excitations carrying net momentum. We analytically calculate the first few Lanczos coefficients and the early time behaviour of the spread complexity associated with these states. Then, using numerical methods, we obtain the coefficients reaching larger Krylov indices and find the associated spread complexity for a longer range of time evolution. We also compare the rate of change of the resulting spread complexity with the proposed holographic dual quantity, related to the proper momentum of an infalling particle in the dual bulk, but we observe a mismatch.

papers.title_en: Orientation-Dependent Casimir Energy and Generalized Torque in Lorentz-Violating Rectangular Compactifications
papers.abstract_en: We derive the renormalized Casimir energy of a free massive real scalar field on the rectangular compactification \(\mathbb{R}^{1,r}\times T^p\) in the presence of a constant CPT-even aether-like Lorentz-violating background. Allowing the spatial part of the background vector to have an arbitrary orientation relative to the compactification lattice, we characterize the resulting orientation-dependent geometric response of the vacuum. Integrating out the noncompact momenta reduces the effective spatial kinetic matrix to its Schur complement, and Poisson resummation yields a closed, exponentially convergent Bessel-function lattice sum within the stability domain. The resulting expression separates an orientation-independent kinetic normalization, \([1+λu_μu^μ]^{-1/2}\), from an orientation-dependent deformation of the image-lattice metric. Coordinate-aligned configurations are recovered as special cases, and the exact massless limit and the compact-direction pressures are obtained. For a two-dimensional compact subspace, we explicitly analyze the angular dependence of the vacuum energy and derive the associated generalized Casimir torque. These results establish how the relative orientation between a Lorentz-violating background and an anisotropic compactification lattice enters the renormalized vacuum energy and its directional response.

papers.title_en: mm-jets in the multi-messenger era
papers.abstract_en: Jets and outflows operate across the full cosmic mass scale from young stellar objects (YSOs) and X-ray binaries (XRBs) to active galactic nuclei (AGN), gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), and tidal disruption events (TDEs), shaping many time-domain and multi-messenger transients. Key questions concern on how jets are launched, accelerated and collimated; where and how they dissipate energy and accelerate particles; and how they couple to their environments to set electromagnetic counterpart diversity and feedback. Millimeter and sub-millimeter observations uniquely address these questions by tracking the evolving synchrotron turnover for robust calorimetry and Lorentz-factor constraints, providing full-Stokes polarization and Faraday diagnostics close to the jet base, and enabling high-resolution imaging from Galactic ejecta to event-horizon-scale AGN jet bases via global Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI). We describe the jet and outflow science enabled by ALMA2040, a next-generation mm/sub-mm interferometer combining an order-of-magnitude sensitivity gain with rapid-response observing, simultaneous multi-band coverage, full-Stokes polarimetry, and integration with global VLBI networks. These capabilities will enable statistically controlled, trigger-driven samples spanning XRB outbursts, early GRB afterglows, protostellar disk winds and jet launching, AGN jet bases, and jetted TDEs, establishing mm/sub-mm astronomy as a cornerstone of time-domain and multi-messenger jet physics in the 2040s and beyond.

papers.title_en: Understanding cosmic explosions
papers.abstract_en: Millimeter-wavelength observations provide a uniquely sensitive window into the physics of cosmic explosions, from supernovae (SNe) and tidal disruption events (TDEs) to nova eruptions, stellar mergers and electromagnetic counterparts to gravitational wave (GW) sources. Over the past decade, discoveries across the transient sky have revealed that many of the most informative phases of shock interaction, particle acceleration and jet formation unfold at frequencies above the traditional cm-wave domain, where synchrotron self-absorption weakens and thermal, nonthermal and dust components can be disentangled. Upcoming wide-field mm surveys will detect a new population of short-lived transients but will be limited by coarse localization and limited spectral characterization. ALMA2040, with dramatically improved sensitivity, wide instantaneous spectral coverage, rapid-response and sub-arraying modes, polarimetry and extended baselines, is essential for converting these discoveries into robust physical constraints. Here we outline the scientific context, key open questions and the ALMA2040 capabilities required to unlock the full potential of millimeter time-domain astrophysics in the 2040s.

papers.title_en: Quantum oscillations in a solvable model of a Kondo insulator
papers.abstract_en: We study the effects of interactions on the low-energy density of states (SdH) and magnetization (dHvA) quantum oscillations (QOs) in a Kondo insulator. Toward this end we introduce a generalization of the periodic Anderson model with Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) interactions at each site that is exactly solvable in the large-$N$ limit, where $N$ is the number of flavors of the heavy $f$ electrons. We show analytically and numerically that the insulating state remains stable in terms of spectrum, thermodynamics, and transport at low temperatures even for interaction strengths much larger than non-interacting band gap of the hybridization-gap insulator. We analytically derive generalizations of Lifshitz-Kosevich (LK) formulae, distinct for the SdH and dHvA QOs, for the interacting insulator. We find that the SdH oscillation frequencies, $F_0\pm δF$, corresponding to the conduction and valence band edges, can be weakly renormalized by interaction relative to their non-interacting values. In contrast, dHvA QO frequency $F_0$ is not renormalized by interactions, and remains the same as that for the non-interacting unhybridized bands. The QO amplitudes show a remarkable difference: the dHvA amplitude is essentially unaffected by interactions, while the SdH amplitude is strongly enhanced due to gap renormalization.

papers.title_en: Compact Dark Matter with Globular Cluster Pulsars
papers.abstract_en: Pulsars are exceptionally stable clocks, and a compact dark-matter object passing near the line of sight to a pulsar delays its pulses through the Shapiro effect. The number of detectable transits is set by the integral over the dark-matter density along the line of sight connecting the Earth and the pulsar. Established pulsars in pulsar timing arrays are typically within one kiloparsec of the Earth and hence sit in a dark-matter density comparable to our local value. In this work, we explore globular clusters in the inner Galaxy as targets to search for compact dark matter. These high-pulsar-density environments can be cheaply observed with a single telescope beam and enjoy a large dark-matter crossing rate. Additionally, since the recently detected nanohertz gravitational-wave background is nearly common to the cluster's pulsars, a multi-pulsar analysis can remove much of its contribution. Ranking known clusters, we find that Terzan 5, with 49 pulsars, offers the best reach. A forty-year campaign of weekly four-hour visits at the sensitivity envisioned for the second phase of the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) would probe compact objects making up $6\%$ of the dark matter at $0.02\,M_\odot$. Finally, we estimate the foreground from stars and stellar remnants in Terzan 5 and along the sightline. It is subdominant near the most sensitive low-mass part of the SKA benchmark, but becomes important over parts of the stellar mass range.

papers.title_en: A model for the ongoing subcluster interaction in Centaurus
papers.abstract_en: Intracluster globular clusters (GCs) preserve the hierarchical and chemical history of galaxy cluster assembly. The nearby Centaurus cluster is believed to be undergoing an interaction between two subclusters, Cen 30 and Cen 45, which should leave an imprint on its intracluster GCs. We aim to characterise the GC population in Centaurus and constrain its recent assembly history, ultimately constructing an interaction scenario consistent with the observational evidence. Using deep VLT/FORS imaging in the $V$ and $I$ bands, we select GC candidates around the cluster centre based on morphology and colour criteria. We use a Voronoi tessellation approach to study the GC spatial distribution and density profiles, demonstrating its advantages over traditional annuli-based methods. We then constrain the evolution of the galaxy luminosity function using the GC specific frequency and colour distribution. The GC spatial distribution shows significant substructure. As in other clusters, red GCs are concentrated on the brightest galaxies, whereas blue GCs trace a more extended structure. We confirm and quantify the previously reported 'bridge' of GCs connecting NGC 4696 and NGC 4709, showing that it hosts twice as many GCs as expected from the projected GC systems of the two galaxies alone. The inferred evolution of the galaxy luminosity function agrees with previous results for Hydra I, yielding a faint-end slope of $α=-1.87_{-0.06}^{+0.06}$ for the galaxy population that assembled the Centaurus core. We propose a nearly head-on collision scenario in which Cen 45 recently passed through Cen 30, with the two subclusters moving approximately along the line of sight. This scenario explains the large line-of-sight velocity difference between the subclusters, the hot X-ray-emitting gas between them, the GC bridge, and the puffed-up GC system of NGC 4709.

papers.title_en: Leptogenesis with a GeV-Scale Quasi-Dirac Neutrino
papers.abstract_en: We discuss leptogenesis in a model with a GeV-scale quasi-Dirac neutral lepton, comprising mainly sterile states, which is accessible to future experiments. In particular, we show that Higgs-decay leptogenesis can naturally arise from the type-I seesaw mechanism with spontaneously broken global lepton number together with a discrete $Z_2$ symmetry, yielding two quasi-degenerate right-handed neutrinos (RHNs) which, to excellent approximation, form a single Dirac neutrino, with a tiny mass splitting as required for resonant enhancement generated by higher-dimensional lepton-number-violating operators. Incorporating finite-temperature effects, we show that the observed baryon asymmetry can be successfully generated through thermal Higgs decays for 0.1-10 GeV mass quasi-Dirac neutrinos, with the CP asymmetry arising from the interplay between the vacuum and thermal contributions to the mass splitting. In the parameter region of successful leptogenesis, the quasi-Dirac neutrino is accessible to future heavy neutral lepton searches at SHiP, MATHUSLA and FCC-ee. In addition, the same symmetry-breaking sector gives rise to unstable domain walls whose annihilation can generate a stochastic gravitational-wave background, providing a complementary probe of the framework.

papers.title_en: Boundary-induced geometrical frustration in a square Rydberg-atom lattice
papers.abstract_en: We study geometric defects in square-lattice Rydberg-atom arrays induced by lattice-size parity in the striated density-wave phase. While odd-sized lattices select a single striated domain, even-sized lattices seed incompatible domains at the four corners, resulting in a π/2-rotation invariant state with a geometrical defect emanating from the lattice center. At larger detunings, we instead identify a π-rotation-invariant state with two domains nucleated by opposite corners and separated by a one-dimensional diagonal defect. We probe the state-preparation protocol on the Aquila atomic quantum processor and benchmark it with equilibrium and real-time dynamics tensor-network simulations. Our results assess the role of boundaries and lattice size in determining the global ordering in programmable quantum matter.

papers.title_en: Wandering intermediate-mass black holes and off-nuclear tidal disruption events from early star clusters
papers.abstract_en: Off-nuclear tidal disruption events (TDEs) reveal evidence for massive black holes outside galactic centers, but the origins of this wandering population remain uncertain. We investigate wandering intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs) formed through runaway stellar collisions in dense, high-redshift star clusters and predict their TDE signatures across cosmic time. Our semi-analytic model samples clusters associated with low-mass subhalos at $7<z<20$ and uses merger trees from the IllustrisTNG TNG50 simulation to follow the assembly of 15 elliptical galaxies with stellar masses of $10^9-10^{11}~M_\odot$. We compare two models for high-redshift cluster formation: a maximal model taken from a high-resolution simulation and a conservative model calibrated from local cluster relations. Off-nuclear TDEs produced through this mechanism occur in bursts within 10-100 Myr of IMBH formation as the loss-cone surrounding the black hole is depleted. We estimate the rate of off-nuclear TDEs expected across time per galaxy, and characterize these events as typically occurring between $10-10^3$ kpc from their host galaxy centers. Event rates increase with galaxy mass; in the maximal model, the progenitors of the most massive galaxies reach peak off-nuclear TDE rates of approximately $5\times10^{-4}-4\times10^{-2}~\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ per galaxy at $7\lesssim z\lesssim13$. This work provides a framework for constraining the early population of star clusters that form IMBHs through runaway collapse via their contribution to the rate of off-nuclear TDEs in the high redshift Universe.

papers.title_en: 6d SCFTs and terminal singularities
papers.abstract_en: The classification of 6d $\mathcal{N}=(1,0)$ SCFTs has been carried out with great success, enumerating consistent elliptically fibered threefolds in F-theory. In this note, we observe that the E-string 6d SCFT can be decorated with extra matter sectors. This decoration exploits an opening allowed by the current classification, implementing terminal singularities nested on the curve of the base of the elliptic fibration that supplies the tensor branch. Additionally, via dimensional reduction on a circle, we identify versions of the 5d $E_n$ theories decorated by extra matter sectors. As a bonus, the end of the resulting RG flow cascade reproduces a 5d theory recently constructed in the literature, explaining its 6d origin. We remain agnostic as to whether the decorated 6d and 5d theories constitute novel SCFTs.

papers.title_en: Nonlocal Gravity, Restricted CPL Dynamics and DESI Constraints
papers.abstract_en: Nonlocal modifications of gravity provide a theoretically motivated framework in which cosmic acceleration can emerge dynamically without introducing a fundamental cosmological constant. We revisit the cosmological predictions of the Maggiore--Mancarella nonlocal $R\,\Box^{-2}R$ model, with particular emphasis on its background dynamics and observational viability in light of recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation measurements. A key feature of the theory is its predictive character: for fixed standard cosmological parameters, each value of the nonlocal parameter determines a specific effective pair $(w_0,w_a)$, so that the model traces a restricted trajectory in the Chevallier--Polarski--Linder plane rather than spanning the full phenomenological parameter space. We construct this mapping explicitly and confront the model with observations by implementing its cosmological dynamics in a Boltzmann solver and performing a Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis using Cosmic Microwave Background, supernova, and DESI BAO data. We find that current datasets constrain the nonlocal parameter close to the $Λ$CDM limit, with no statistically significant preference for nonlocal deviations.

papers.title_en: The unified Bound Dark Energy--Bound Dark Matter model: theory and constraints from DESI DR2
papers.abstract_en: The unified Bound Dark Energy--Bound Dark Matter (BDE-BDM) model derives both the dark energy and the whole of the dark matter from a single supersymmetric $SU(3)$ gauge group with $N_f=6$ flavors. Gauge-coupling unification predicts the scale at which it condenses, $\Lc=34^{+16}_{-11}$~eV, before any cosmological data are used, so the dark-energy sector adds no parameter to those of \LCDM\ and the dark-matter sector adds only one. Fitting DESI DR2 BAO, Planck CMB, Planck+ACT DR6 CMB lensing, and three supernova compilations (PantheonPlus, Union3.1, DES-Dovekie) gives, for Union3.1, $\Lc=43.67\pm0.13$~eV, inside the predicted range: a high-energy prediction met by a late-time measurement. The equation of state evolves to $w_0=-0.9262\pm0.0005$ and never crosses the phantom divide. Relative to \LCDM\ the model lowers the DESI BAO $χ^2$ by $2.95$--$3.67$ and the supernova $χ^2$ by $2.53$--$4.07$, recovering $57\%$--$71\%$ of the total reduction that \wowa\ obtains by fitting two dark-energy parameters to the same data, and reaching the lower BAO $χ^2$ of the two models for two of the three compilations. Its $Δ\mathrm{DIC}$ against \LCDM\ is strong for every compilation, $-8.28$ to $-7.47$, varying by $0.81$ where that of \wowa\ varies by $4.8$. Because the dark-energy sector adds no parameter to those of \LCDM, the likelihood gain survives the Occam penalty: $\ln B=+4.09$, $+4.12$, and $+4.83$ against \LCDM, where \wowa\ gives $-2.11$, $-0.26$, and $-0.56$. Among six models pairing a cosmological constant, the \wowa\ parametrization or bound dark energy with cold or bound dark matter, BDE-BDM has the largest Bayesian evidence.

papers.title_en: Surviving readout errors and incomplete postselection in monitored quantum circuits
papers.abstract_en: We study how readout errors affect dynamics in monitored quantum circuits. Such errors make postselection effectively incomplete, conditioning trajectories on imperfect rather than true records. Focusing on U(1)-symmetric circuits, we find that the charge-sharpening transition survives at a finite error rate, with the sharp phase's vanishing fluctuations replaced by a finite steady-state plateau. The charge fluctuations show a shallow minimum near the ideal transition point as a function of measurement rate, signaling the competition between measurement-induced purification and noise-induced mixing. By decomposing the fluctuations into quantum and classical contributions, we show the minimum marks where incomplete postselection still retains enough trajectory memory to attenuate noise-induced mixing, leaving a detectable signature of the transition even in a noisy setting. Mid-circuit measurements are far harder to mitigate against readout errors than standard end-of-circuit ones, because the errors corrupt the postselection itself; the decomposition therefore offers a minimal mitigation framework and a route to locate the transition directly from experimental data. Our results show that charge sharpening survives readout errors in a quantitative and experimentally accessible way.

papers.title_en: All-temperature superfluidity in two dimensions
papers.abstract_en: In local theories with short-range interactions, continuous symmetries cannot be spontaneously broken in two spatial dimensions at nonzero temperature. $\mathrm{U}(1)$-symmetric models instead admit a Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) phase with quasi-long-range order and nonzero phase stiffness, which is normally destroyed at high temperatures by vortex proliferation. Here, we show that a BKT phase, and with it superfluidity, can persist to arbitrarily high temperatures. Using the large-$N$ expansion, we study a $(2+1)$-dimensional quantum field theory in which a complex scalar is coupled to the critical $\mathrm{O}(N)$ model. At the biconical fixed point, where the inter-sector coupling is negative, the thermal effective potential has a circle of minima with nonzero $\mathrm{U}(1)$ amplitude. Integrating out the gapped fluctuations yields an effective theory for the compact phase mode at distances large compared to $1/T$. Since temperature is the only scale at the fixed point, the phase stiffness grows linearly with temperature, with a proportionality factor that scales linearly with $N$ and is fixed entirely by the fixed point. This renders vortex operators irrelevant for sufficiently large $N$. We further show that the vortex fugacity is exponentially small in $N$.

papers.title_en: Gluon Scattering in Expanding de Sitter Universe
papers.abstract_en: We construct an observer-centric S-matrix in the expanding Poincaré patch of four-dimensional de Sitter space. The asymptotic states are defined along the worldline of a comoving, or eternal, observer, the only kind of geodesic observer that remains in the patch for all proper time, and the free Hamiltonian is the conserved charge generating translations in her proper time. The resulting S-matrix is independent of which eternal observer is chosen. We apply the construction to pure Yang--Mills theory in Coulomb gauge and compute the three- and four-gluon amplitudes at tree level. The amplitudes have a structure similar to the cosmological correlators of gauge currents and are constrained by the Ward identities of de Sitter isometries.

papers.title_en: Probing ordered magnetic fields in galaxies across cosmic time
papers.abstract_en: Magnetic fields are dynamically important across many astronomical environments, yet their origin, strength, and evolution over cosmic time remain poorly understood. Ordered magnetic fields are ubiquitous in the nearby Universe, as revealed by a range of observational techniques, but evidence for their existence at cosmological distances is scarce. Recent ALMA detections of polarised dust emission indicate that galactic-scale ordered magnetic fields, spanning up to kiloparsec scales, were already present in massive star-forming galaxies at redshifts up to $z\sim5.6$. This white paper argues that the ALMA2040 concept -- with its nearly tenfold improvement in sensitivity and angular resolution, and full-polarisation capability extended to higher-frequency bands -- will open up the study of cosmic magnetism in the early Universe. We identify four science drivers: constraining the dynamos that generate galactic-scale ordered fields, measuring the strength of early magnetic fields, connecting magnetic fields to galaxy evolution across cosmic time, and constraining dust grain properties through the polarised spectral energy distribution. We summarise the corresponding requirements in angular resolution, spectral coverage, and sensitivity, and discuss synergies with next-generation telescopes.

papers.title_en: How Little Red Dots Turn Blue: Evolution of Kelvin-Helmholtz Contracting Black Hole Envelopes and Observational Diagnostics
papers.abstract_en: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations have revealed compact, red-colored, broad-line emitters known as little red dots (LRDs), while a bluer counterpart population has been referred to as little blue dots (LBDs). Their physical connection remains unclear: they may represent different evolutionary stages of the same phenomenon, distinct populations, or different phases of the broader evolution of early galaxies and their black holes (BHs). We propose a model in which a rapidly growing BH is embedded in a geometrically thick gaseous envelope accompanied by concurrent nuclear star formation. The model reproduces the observed spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of LRDs and LBDs, and naturally connects the two phases through Kelvin-Helmholtz contraction of the envelope and exposure of the nuclear accretion disk, as the gas supply declines due to external stellar activity or feedback. We predict the corresponding evolutionary tracks in the UV-optical slope ($β_{\rm UV}$-$β_{\rm opt}$) plane which bridge the apparent gap between LRDs and LBDs. These evolutionary tracks start from the LRD regime and consistently exhibit a red excursion that extends toward $(β_{\rm UV},β_{\rm opt})\sim(2,-1)$ before turning toward the LBD regime. This feature is largely insensitive to variations in the model parameters that govern the envelope structure, providing a robust signature of the transitional population. The transition lasts $\sim5$-$50\,\mathrm{Myr}$, depending primarily on the BH feedback efficiency and the gas-retention efficiency of the envelope. The abundance ratio of transitional systems to LRDs therefore provides a constraint on BH feedback and gas retention during the rapid growth of early supermassive BHs.

papers.title_en: Towards ultrarelativistic scattering near the light ring: asymptotic divergence of gravitational-wave fluxes
papers.abstract_en: Near the threshold between scattering and capture by a Schwarzschild black hole, a particle spends a long time close to an unstable circular orbit, which in the ultrarelativistic limit approaches the light ring. Here we study the behavior of the gravitational wave fluxes emitted by such an ultrarelativistic particle at first order in the mass ratio. The fluxes radiated to infinity and absorbed by the horizon diverge as the inverse distance from the light ring multiplied by its logarithm. Using the Wentzel, Kramers, and Brillouin (WKB) approximation to solve the Regge-Wheeler equation and treating the infinite harmonic sum analytically, we derive an exact expression for the coefficient of this logarithmic enhancement and show that it is identical for both fluxes. We then estimate the coefficients of the subleading pole contributions by combining numerical calculations at low multipoles with the exact asymptotics at large multipoles. We further conjecture an extension to equatorial circular orbits in Kerr. Interestingly, our results also inform the analytical structure of the energy and angular momentum losses of ultrarelativistic scattering orbits near the light ring. More broadly, our work illustrates how WKB methods can provide the asymptotic behavior of self-force observables in regimes where numerical mode sums become increasingly challenging.

papers.title_en: Tracing small-scale structure formation through cosmic time with strong gravitational lensing: A case for a next-generation sub-millimetre/millimetre interferometer
papers.abstract_en: The nature of dark matter and the growth of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) remain major open questions in modern astrophysics. Both leave a key signature in an overlapping, largely unexplored mass range: $<10^7$ M$_{\odot}$ dark haloes and wandering black holes. These may be undetectable directly, but detectable through gravitational perturbation of strongly lensed images, and partly or entirely distinguishable from one another through lensing data alone. We demonstrate through realistic simulations that a 255-element sub-mm/mm interferometer could probe this critical mass regime, detecting gravitational perturbations in strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) from objects down to at least $10^5$ M$_{\odot}$. Combined with lens-galaxy characterisation from the European Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), which strengthens the physical interpretation of detected perturbers, and the unprecedented lens samples expected from Euclid and the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), this facility could deliver a census of low-mass dark matter haloes and wandering massive black holes across cosmic time.

papers.title_en: Region bounds, error margins and certified positivity in the numerical conformal bootstrap; Or the first mathematically rigorous bounds on the 3d Ising CFT critical exponents
papers.abstract_en: Numerical conformal bootstrap bounds are commonly called rigorous, yet as published they are not theorems: they hold at sampled points rather than on regions of parameter space, for truncated rational approximations of the conformal blocks, for a finite list of spins, and up to floating-point rounding. We close all four gaps. We show how to search efficiently for functionals positive on regions, including external-dimension space; how positivity on the large-spin crossing vectors can be imposed as such a region constraint; how new analytic bounds on the conformal-block recursion relations give functionals positive on the true, untruncated crossing vectors; and how to certify the positivity of these functionals in exact arithmetic. The certification rests on Bernstein-basis positivity certificates in up to three variables, exact arithmetic in $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$, a compactified treatment of the infinite spin tail, and an explicit bound on the difference between the true blocks and their truncations, so that infinitely many positivity conditions reduce to finitely many machine-checked sign conditions. As a flagship application we certify an exclusion region in the $(Δ_σ,Δ_ε)$ plane: for $Δ_σ\in[0.505,0.5405]$ all of $Δ_ε\in(1/2,3]$ is excluded except a small rectangle containing the 3d Ising island, giving rigorous two-sided bounds on the critical exponents $η$ and $ν$ under explicitly stated spectrum assumptions. The analytic inputs for the mixed $σ$-$ε$ system, which would remove the spin-2 gap assumption, are also proved. The same methods prevent common practical failure modes and can make bootstrap searches faster: region bounds turn the mapping of an island into a handful of one-dimensional bisections. The essential code to reproduce the search and the certification, and all machine-checkable certificates, are released.

papers.title_en: The Impact of High-Mass Clusters on the Binary Black Hole Merger Rate over Cosmic Time
papers.abstract_en: We present a cosmological calculation of the binary black hole merger rate from dense star clusters, using a $\texttt{Cluster Monte Carlo}$ ($\texttt{CMC}$) model grid spanning the full observed parameter space of cluster mass, metallicity, and virial radius. For the first time, we incorporate $N=10^{7}$-particle $\texttt{CMC}$ models into this calculation, including a new solar-metallicity model, extending the $\texttt{CMC Cluster Catalog}$ to the most massive clusters observed in the local Universe. Using an analytic cluster formation model which convolves the cluster formation rate with delay-time distributions from our model suite, we find that the local cluster BBH merger rate is dominated by low-mass ($M_1 \lesssim 20\,M_\odot$) mergers originating from recently formed, high-metallicity clusters. While high-mass clusters are the primary sites of hierarchical (second-generation and higher) mergers, their contribution to the overall merger rate is suppressed by the exponential cutoff of the cluster initial mass function. The hierarchical merger rate is therefore highly sensitive to the exact value of the Schechter mass, $M_S$, suggesting that gravitational wave constraints on the hierarchical merger fraction can independently constrain the high-mass end of the cluster initial mass function. Our cluster formation model reproduces the observed present-day GC number density without fine tuning, and we find $M_S = 10^7\,M_\odot$ provides the best match to the observed Virgo GC mass distribution. For this value, $27\%$ of local dynamical mergers are hierarchical, compared to $18\%$ for the canonical value of $M_S = 10^{6.26}\,M_\odot$. Our merger weights, which we make publicly available, can be used for direct comparison with LVK distributions and other formation models.

papers.title_en: Quantum critical collapse in the large $D$ limit
